switch() {
    imgpath="$1"
    mode_flag="$2"
    type_flag="$3"
    color_flag="$4"
    color="$5"

    # Start Gemini auto-categorization if enabled
    aiStylingEnabled=$(jq -r '.background.widgets.clock.cookie.aiStyling' "$SHELL_CONFIG_FILE")
    if [[ "$aiStylingEnabled" == "true" ]]; then
        categorize_wallpaper "$imgpath" &
    fi

    read scale screenx screeny screensizey < <(hyprctl monitors -j | jq '.[] | select(.focused) | .scale, .x, .y, .height' | xargs)
    cursorposx=$(hyprctl cursorpos -j | jq '.x' 2>/dev/null) || cursorposx=960
    cursorposx=$(bc <<< "scale=0; ($cursorposx - $screenx) * $scale / 1")
    cursorposy=$(hyprctl cursorpos -j | jq '.y' 2>/dev/null) || cursorposy=540
    cursorposy=$(bc <<< "scale=0; ($cursorposy - $screeny) * $scale / 1")
    cursorposy_inverted=$((screensizey - cursorposy))

    matugen_args=(--source-color-index 0)

    if [[ "$color_flag" == "1" ]]; then
        matugen_args+=(color hex "$color")
        generate_colors_material_args=(--color "$color")
    else
        if [[ -z "$imgpath" ]]; then
            echo 'Aborted'
            exit 0
        fi

        check_and_prompt_upscale "$imgpath" &
        kill_existing_mpvpaper

        if is_video "$imgpath"; then
            mkdir -p "$THUMBNAIL_DIR"

            missing_deps=()
            if ! command -v mpvpaper &> /dev/null; then
                missing_deps+=("mpvpaper")
            fi
            if ! command -v ffmpeg &> /dev/null; then
                missing_deps+=("ffmpeg")
            fi
            if [ ${#missing_deps[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
                echo "Missing deps: ${missing_deps[*]}"
                echo "Arch: sudo pacman -S ${missing_deps[*]}"
                action=$(notify-send \
                    -a "Wallpaper switcher" \
                    -c "im.error" \
                    -A "install_arch=Install (Arch)" \
                    "Can't switch to video wallpaper" \
                    "Missing dependencies: ${missing_deps[*]}")
                if [[ "$action" == "install_arch" ]]; then
                    kitty -1 sudo pacman -S "${missing_deps[*]}"
                    if command -v mpvpaper &>/dev/null && command -v ffmpeg &>/dev/null; then
                        notify-send 'Wallpaper switcher' 'Alright, try again!' -a "Wallpaper switcher"
                    fi
                fi
                exit 0
            fi

            # Set wallpaper path
            set_wallpaper_path "$imgpath"

            # Set video wallpaper
            local video_path="$imgpath"
            monitors=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[] | .name')
            for monitor in $monitors; do
                mpvpaper -o "$VIDEO_OPTS" "$monitor" "$video_path" &
                sleep 0.1
            done

            # Extract first frame for color generation
            thumbnail="$THUMBNAIL_DIR/$(basename "$imgpath").jpg"
            ffmpeg -y -i "$imgpath" -vframes 1 "$thumbnail" 2>/dev/null

            # Set thumbnail path
            set_thumbnail_path "$thumbnail"

            if [ -f "$thumbnail" ]; then
                matugen_args+=(image "$thumbnail")
                generate_colors_material_args=(--path "$thumbnail")
                create_restore_script "$video_path"
            else
                echo "Cannot create image to colorgen"
                remove_restore
                exit 1
            fi
        else
            matugen_args+=(image "$imgpath")
            generate_colors_material_args=(--path "$imgpath")
            # Update wallpaper path in config
            set_wallpaper_path "$imgpath"
            remove_restore
        fi
    fi

    # Determine mode if not set
    if [[ -z "$mode_flag" ]]; then
        current_mode=$(gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme 2>/dev/null | tr -d "'")
        if [[ "$current_mode" == "prefer-dark" ]]; then
            mode_flag="dark"
        else
            mode_flag="light"
        fi
    fi

    # enforce dark mode for terminal
    if [[ -n "$mode_flag" ]]; then
        matugen_args+=(--mode "$mode_flag")
        if [[ $(jq -r '.appearance.wallpaperTheming.terminalGenerationProps.forceDarkMode' "$SHELL_CONFIG_FILE") == "true" ]]; then
            generate_colors_material_args+=(--mode "dark")
        else
            generate_colors_material_args+=(--mode "$mode_flag")
        fi
    fi
    [[ -n "$type_flag" ]] && matugen_args+=(--type "$type_flag") && generate_colors_material_args+=(--scheme "$type_flag")
    generate_colors_material_args+=(--termscheme "$terminalscheme" --blend_bg_fg)
    generate_colors_material_args+=(--cache "$STATE_DIR/user/generated/color.txt")

    pre_process "$mode_flag"

    # Check if app and shell theming is enabled in config
    if [ -f "$SHELL_CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
        enable_apps_shell=$(jq -r '.appearance.wallpaperTheming.enableAppsAndShell' "$SHELL_CONFIG_FILE")
        if [ "$enable_apps_shell" == "false" ]; then
            echo "App and shell theming disabled, skipping matugen and color generation"
            return
        fi
    fi

    # Set harmony and related properties
    if [ -f "$SHELL_CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
        harmony=$(jq -r '.appearance.wallpaperTheming.terminalGenerationProps.harmony' "$SHELL_CONFIG_FILE")
        harmonize_threshold=$(jq -r '.appearance.wallpaperTheming.terminalGenerationProps.harmonizeThreshold' "$SHELL_CONFIG_FILE")
        term_fg_boost=$(jq -r '.appearance.wallpaperTheming.terminalGenerationProps.termFgBoost' "$SHELL_CONFIG_FILE")
        [[ "$harmony" != "null" && -n "$harmony" ]] && generate_colors_material_args+=(--harmony "$harmony")
        [[ "$harmonize_threshold" != "null" && -n "$harmonize_threshold" ]] && generate_colors_material_args+=(--harmonize_threshold "$harmonize_threshold")
        [[ "$term_fg_boost" != "null" && -n "$term_fg_boost" ]] && generate_colors_material_args+=(--term_fg_boost "$term_fg_boost")
    fi

    matugen "${matugen_args[@]}"
    source "$(eval echo $ILLOGICAL_IMPULSE_VIRTUAL_ENV)/bin/activate"
    python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/generate_colors_material.py" "${generate_colors_material_args[@]}" \
        > "$STATE_DIR"/user/generated/material_colors.scss
    deactivate
    "$SCRIPT_DIR"/applycolor.sh

    # Pass screen width, height, and wallpaper path to post_process
    max_width_desired="$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq '([.[].width] | min)' | xargs)"
    max_height_desired="$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq '([.[].height] | min)' | xargs)"
    post_process "$max_width_desired" "$max_height_desired" "$imgpath"
}

#!/bin/bash
# Usage: set-wallpaper.sh /path/to/image-or-video [transition]
# Applies the wallpaper to every monitor Yin knows about.

WALLPAPER="$1"
TRANSITION="$2"   # optional, e.g. zoom / bookflip (see `yinctl --list-trans`)
[ -z "$WALLPAPER" ] && { echo "Usage: $0 <path> [transition]"; exit 1; }

# Build the optional --trans flag only when a transition was given.
trans_args=()
[ -n "$TRANSITION" ] && trans_args=(--trans "$TRANSITION")

# Discover monitors from yin's per-monitor state files in ~/.cache/yin.
# Cached media is named "<W>x<H>_<file>"; anything else is a monitor name.
monitors=$(ls ~/.cache/yin 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '^[0-9]+x[0-9]+_')

args=()
# Set the wallpaper via yin's IPC on every monitor (fall back to yin's
# default target if none are discovered yet, e.g. on a fresh cache).
if [ -z "$monitors" ]; then
  yinctl --img "$WALLPAPER" "${trans_args[@]}"
else
  while IFS= read -r m; do
    args+=("$m")
  done <<< "$monitors"
fi

for a in "${args[@]}"; do
  yinctl --img "$WALLPAPER" "${trans_args[@]}" --output "$a" &
done
wait

# Regenerate the colour scheme for this wallpaper. Use an absolute path so this
# works regardless of the caller's working directory (e.g. a Hyprland keybind).
# Videos ship a pre-baked matugen JSON (matugen can't sample a video frame);
# images without one derive their palette live from the file.
wp_file="${WALLPAPER##*/}"
wp_stem="${wp_file%%.*}"
colors_json="$HOME/.config/hypr/matugen-colors/$wp_stem.json"
if [ -f "$colors_json" ]; then
  matugen json "$colors_json"
elif [ -f "$WALLPAPER" ] && file --mime-type -b "$WALLPAPER" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^image/'; then
  matugen image "$WALLPAPER"
else
  echo "set-wallpaper: no matugen palette for '$wp_stem' and '$WALLPAPER' is not an image; skipping colours" >&2
fi


# Track current wallpaper for restarts
ln -sf "$WALLPAPER" ~/.cache/current-wallpaper

#!/usr/bin/env bash

## Author : Aditya Shakya (adi1090x)
## Github : @adi1090x
#
## Rofi   : Launcher (Modi Drun, Run, File Browser, Window)
#
## Available Styles
#
## style-1     style-2     style-3     style-4     style-5
## style-6     style-7     style-8     style-9     style-10
## style-11    style-12    style-13    style-14    style-15
#
## Usage:
##   rofi.sh                      # default: app launcher (drun)
##   rofi.sh file1 file2 dir/*    # show the given files/entries, open the picked one
##   find . -type f | rofi.sh     # show piped lines, print the picked one to stdout
##
## In file/dmenu mode: if the chosen entry is an existing path it is opened with
## xdg-open; otherwise the chosen line is printed to stdout (pipe-friendly).

dir="$HOME/.config/rofi/launchers/type-1"
theme='style-6'

## Logging ---------------------------------------------------------------------
log_dir="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/rofi"
log_file="$log_dir/rofi-launcher.log"
mkdir -p "$log_dir" 2>/dev/null

log() {
    # $1 = level, $2 = message
    printf '%s [%s] %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$1" "$2" >>"$log_file"
}

## Collect input: positional args first, otherwise piped stdin ----------------
input=""
if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
    input="$(printf '%s\n' "$@")"
elif [ ! -t 0 ]; then
    # stdin is not a terminal (piped/redirected) -> read whatever was given
    input="$(cat)"
fi

## File / dmenu mode -----------------------------------------------------------
if [ -n "$input" ]; then
    count="$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | grep -c .)"
    log INFO "dmenu mode: showing $count entr$([ "$count" = "1" ] && echo y || echo ies)"

    selection="$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | rofi \
        -dmenu \
        -i \
        -p "files" \
        -theme "${dir}/${theme}.rasi")"
    rc=$?

    if [ -z "$selection" ]; then
        log INFO "dmenu closed with no selection (rc=$rc)"
        exit 0
    fi

    if [ -e "$selection" ]; then
        if xdg-open "$selection" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            log INFO "opened: $selection"
        else
            log ERROR "xdg-open failed for: $selection"
            exit 1
        fi
    else
        # Not an existing path: emit the choice so callers/pipes can consume it
        printf '%s\n' "$selection"
        log WARNING "selection is not an existing path, printed to stdout: $selection"
    fi
    exit 0
fi

log INFO "drun mode (app launcher)"
rofi \
    -show drun \
    -theme "${dir}/${theme}.rasi"

1:#!/bin/bash
2:# Applies the boot wallpaper once yin's IPC daemon is actually ready.
3:#
4:# yin is started by Hyprland's autostart (see hyprland.lua) immediately before
5:# this script. yin binds a Unix socket at /tmp/yin when it comes up, so instead
6:# of guessing with a fixed delay we wait for that socket to exist.
7:#
8:# The target monitors are discovered from the *running* Hyprland via hyprctl
9:# rather than hardcoded: a physical session reports eDP-1 / HDMI-A-1, while a
10:# nested Hyprland reports a virtual output (e.g. WL-1). Hardcoding eDP-1 made
11:# yinctl abort with "Could not find required monitor" and left the screen black.
12:
13:set -u
14:
15:SOCKET="/tmp/yin"
16:IMG="/home/krubics/.config/hypr/images/latios-latias.jpg"
17:LOG="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/hypr/wallpaper-autostart.log"
18:
19:SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS=5000   # give up waiting for the socket after ~5s
20:RETRIES=20               # then retry the apply loop this many times (0.1s apart)
21:POLL_MS=100
22:
23:mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"
24:
25:log() {
26:    printf '%s [wallpaper-autostart] %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$1" >> "$LOG"
27:}
28:
29:log "starting; waiting for yin socket at $SOCKET (timeout ${SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS}ms)"
30:
31:# 1. Wait for yin to create its IPC socket.
32:waited=0
33:while [ ! -S "$SOCKET" ]; do
34:    if [ "$waited" -ge "$SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS" ]; then
35:        log "ERROR: yin socket did not appear within ${SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS}ms; aborting"
36:        exit 1
37:    fi
38:    sleep 0.1
39:    waited=$((waited + POLL_MS))
40:done
41:log "yin socket ready after ${waited}ms"
42:
43:# 2. Discover the monitors this Hyprland instance actually has.
44:monitors=$(hyprctl monitors -j 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].name' 2>/dev/null)
45:if [ -z "$monitors" ]; then
46:    log "WARN: hyprctl reported no monitors; falling back to yin's default output"
47:fi
48:
49:# 3. Apply the wallpaper to each monitor, retrying until every one succeeds.
50:#    Capture rc immediately after yinctl (a no-else 'if' would return 0 instead).
51:attempt=1
52:while :; do
53:    all_ok=1
54:    if [ -z "$monitors" ]; then
55:        yinctl --img "$IMG" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
56:        [ "$?" -ne 0 ] && all_ok=0
57:    else
58:        while IFS= read -r mon; do
59:            [ -z "$mon" ] && continue
60:            yinctl --img "$IMG" --output "$mon" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
61:            rc=$?
62:            if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
63:                all_ok=0
64:                log "yinctl for '$mon' failed (rc=$rc) on attempt ${attempt}"
65:            fi
66:        done <<< "$monitors"
67:    fi
68:
69:    if [ "$all_ok" -eq 1 ]; then
70:        log "wallpaper applied on attempt ${attempt} (img=$IMG; monitors=[$(echo $monitors | tr '\n' ' ')])"
71:        exit 0
72:    fi
73:    if [ "$attempt" -ge "$RETRIES" ]; then
74:        log "ERROR: wallpaper apply failed after ${attempt} attempts"
75:        exit 1
76:    fi
77:    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
78:    sleep 0.1
79:done

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"

log() {
    printf '%s [wallpaper-autostart] %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$1" >> "$LOG"
}

log "starting; waiting for yin socket at $SOCKET (timeout ${SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS}ms)"

# 1. Wait for yin to create its IPC socket.
waited=0
while [ ! -S "$SOCKET" ]; do
    if [ "$waited" -ge "$SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS" ]; then
        log "ERROR: yin socket did not appear within ${SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS}ms; aborting"
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 0.1
    waited=$((waited + POLL_MS))
done
log "yin socket ready after ${waited}ms"

# 2. Discover the monitors this Hyprland instance actually has.
monitors=$(hyprctl monitors -j 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].name' 2>/dev/null)
if [ -z "$monitors" ]; then
    log "WARN: hyprctl reported no monitors; falling back to yin's default output"
fi

# 3. Apply the wallpaper to each monitor, retrying until every one succeeds.
#    Capture rc immediately after yinctl (a no-else 'if' would return 0 instead).
attempt=1
while :; do
    all_ok=1
    if [ -z "$monitors" ]; then
        yinctl --img "$IMG" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
        [ "$?" -ne 0 ] && all_ok=0
    else
        while IFS= read -r mon; do
            [ -z "$mon" ] && continue
            yinctl --img "$IMG" --output "$mon" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
            rc=$?
            if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
                all_ok=0
                log "yinctl for '$mon' failed (rc=$rc) on attempt ${attempt}"
            fi
        done <<< "$monitors"
    fi

    if [ "$all_ok" -eq 1 ]; then
        log "wallpaper applied on attempt ${attempt} (img=$IMG; monitors=[$(echo $monitors | tr '\n' ' ')])"
        exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -ge "$RETRIES" ]; then
        log "ERROR: wallpaper apply failed after ${attempt} attempts"
        exit 1
    fi
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# /* ---- 💫 https://github.com/JaKooLit 💫 ---- */
# This script for selecting wallpapers (SUPER W)

# WALLPAPERS PATH
terminal=kitty
PICTURES_DIR="$(xdg-user-dir PICTURES 2>/dev/null || echo "$HOME/Pictures")"
wallDIR="$PICTURES_DIR/wallpapers"
SCRIPTSDIR="$HOME/.config/hypr/scripts"
wallpaper_current="$HOME/.config/hypr/wallpaper_effects/.wallpaper_current"

# Directory for swaync
iDIR="$HOME/.config/swaync/images"
iDIRi="$HOME/.config/swaync/icons"

# swww transition config
FPS=60
TYPE="any"
DURATION=2
BEZIER=".43,1.19,1,.4"
SWWW_PARAMS="--transition-fps $FPS --transition-type $TYPE --transition-duration $DURATION --transition-bezier $BEZIER"

# Check if package bc exists
if ! command -v bc &>/dev/null; then
…
fi

# Variables
rofi_theme="$HOME/.config/rofi/config-wallpaper.rasi"
focused_monitor=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[] | select(.focused) | .name')

# Ensure focused_monitor is detected
if [[ -z "$focused_monitor" ]]; then
…
fi

# Monitor details
scale_factor=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r --arg mon "$focused_monitor" '.[] | select(.name == $mon) | .scale')
monitor_height=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r --arg mon "$focused_monitor" '.[] | select(.name == $mon) | .height')

icon_size=$(echo "scale=1; ($monitor_height * 3) / ($scale_factor * 150)" | bc)
adjusted_icon_size=$(echo "$icon_size" | awk '{if ($1 < 15) $1 = 20; if ($1 > 25) $1 = 25; print $1}')
rofi_override="element-icon{size:${adjusted_icon_size}%;}"

# Kill existing wallpaper daemons for video
kill_wallpaper_for_video() { … }

# Kill existing wallpaper daemons for image
kill_wallpaper_for_image() { … }

# Retrieve wallpapers (both images & videos)
mapfile -d '' PICS < <(find -L "${wallDIR}" -type f \( \
  -iname "*.jpg" -o -iname "*.jpeg" -o -iname "*.png" -o -iname "*.gif" -o \
  -iname "*.bmp" -o -iname "*.tiff" -o -iname "*.webp" -o \
  -iname "*.mp4" -o -iname "*.mkv" -o -iname "*.mov" -o -iname "*.webm" \) -print0)

RANDOM_PIC="${PICS[$((RANDOM % ${#PICS[@]}))]}"
RANDOM_PIC_NAME=". random"

# Rofi command
rofi_command="rofi -i -show -dmenu -config $rofi_theme -theme-str $rofi_override"

# Sorting Wallpapers
menu() { … }


modify_startup_config() { … }

# Apply Image Wallpaper
apply_image_wallpaper() { … }

apply_video_wallpaper() { … }

# Main function
main() { … }

# Check if rofi is already running
if pidof rofi >/dev/null; then
  pkill rofi
fi

I'm getting the full picture of the current setup: `yin` is a wallpaper daemon similar to swww, with a CLI tool `yinctl` that communicates via a socket at `/tmp/yin`, caching per-monitor state in `~/.cache/yin` using filenames like `<W>x<H>_<file>`. The command `yinctl --img <path> --output <monitor> --trans <transition>` handles wallpaper changes, and it's configured to autostart in Hyprland.

lua which then runs `wallpaper-autostart.sh` to wait for the socket and apply wallpapers to each monitor. The `set-wallpaper.sh` script discovers monitors from the cache, calls `yinctl` in parallel for each one, regenerates matugen colors, and tracks the current wallpaper via symlink. The picker keybind at line 138-145 in `keybinds.lua` uses `SUPER+SHIFT+Space` to open a rofi dmenu listing wallpapers from `~/.config/hypr/wallpapers`, looks up the transition type from a Lua table based on filename, then calls `set-wallpaper.sh` with the path and transition. Now I need to replace this entire `yin`/`yinctl` system with `swww` and `swww-daemon` from nixpkgs, building an equivalent picker that maintains the same workflow.

First, I'll install swww via nix profile or home-manager if available, then rewrite the startup sequence to use `swww-daemon` instead of the yin daemon. The `wallpaper-autostart.sh` script needs to wait for swww's socket using `swww query` to check readiness, then apply the boot wallpaper with `swww img`. The `set-wallpaper.sh` script becomes simpler—just call `swww img <path> --transition-type ... --outputs <mon>` for each monitor instead of yinctl. Finally, I'll adjust the transition names in the keybinds and Lua table to match swww's available transition types like fade, left, right, wipe, wave, grow, center, and random instead of yin's bookflip, bounce, box, and other yin-specific transitions.

Since this looks like a non-NixOS system (Ubuntu/Debian based) with nix installed as a package manager, I should check whether home-manager is configured or if packages are managed purely through `nix profile install`.

content.text:
=== swww --help ===
A Solution to your Wayland Wallpaper Woes

Change what your monitors display as a background by controlling the swww daemon at runtime.
Supports animated gifs and putting different stuff in different monitors. I also did my best to make
it as resource efficient as possible.

Note `swww` will only work in a compositor that implements the layer-shell protocol. Typically,
wlr-roots based compositors.

Usage: swww <COMMAND>

Commands:
  clear        Fills the specified outputs with the given color
  restore      Restores the last displayed image on the specified outputs
  clear-cache  Clears the swww cache
  img          Sends an image (or animated gif) for the daemon to display
  pause        Pauses the daemon
  kill         Kills the daemon
  query        Asks the daemon to print output information (names and dimensions)
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

=== swww img --help ===
Sends an image (or animated gif) for the daemon to display.

Use `-` to read from stdin

Usage: swww img [OPTIONS] <IMAGE>

Arguments:
  <IMAGE>
          Path of image or hexcode (starting with 0x) to display

Options:
  -a, --all
          Set the image for all swww-daemon instances (all namespaces)

  -o, --outputs <OUTPUTS>
          Comma separated list of outputs to display the image at.
          
          If it isn't set, the image is displayed on all outputs.
          
          [default: ]

  -n, --namespace <NAMESPACE>
          The daemon's namespace.
          
          The resulting namespace will be 'swww-daemon' appended to what you pass in this argument.
          For this to work, you must call `swww-daemon --namespace <custom_namespace>` with the same
          value you use here.
          
          You can specify multiple namespaces at once with multiple `--namespaces` arguments. The
          commands will be sent to every namespace you have specified.
          
          [default: ]

      --no-resize
          Do not resize the image. Equivalent to `--resize=no`
          
          If this is set, the image won't be resized, and will be centralized in the middle of the
          screen instead. If it is smaller than the screen's size, it will be padded with the value
          of `fill_color`, below.

      --resize <RESIZE>
          Whether to resize the image and the method by which to resize it

          Possible values:
          - no:      Do not resize the image
          - crop:    Resize the image to fill the whole screen, cropping out parts that don't fit
          - fit:     Resize the image to fit inside the screen, preserving the original aspect ratio
          - stretch: Resize the image to fit inside the screen, without preserving the original
            aspect ratio
          
          [default: crop]

      --fill-color <FILL_COLOR>
          Which color to fill the padding with when output image does not fill screen
          
          [default: 000000ff]

  -f, --filter <FILTER>
          Filter to use when scaling images (run swww img --help to see options).
          
          Available options are:
          
          Nearest | Bilinear | CatmullRom | Mitchell | Lanczos3
          
          These are offered by the fast_image_resize crate
          (https://docs.rs/fast_image_resize/2.5.0/fast_image_resize/). 'Nearest' is what I
          recommend for pixel art stuff, and ONLY for pixel art stuff. It is also the fastest
          filter.
          
          For non pixel art stuff, I would usually recommend one of the last three, though some
          experimentation will be necessary to see which one you like best. Also note they are all
          slower than Nearest.
          
          [default: Lanczos3]

  -t, --transition-type <TRANSITION_TYPE>
          Sets the type of transition. Default is 'simple', that fades into the new image
          
          Possible transitions are:
          
          none | simple | fade | left | right | top | bottom | wipe | wave | grow | center | any |
          outer | random
          
          The 'left', 'right', 'top' and 'bottom' options make the transition happen from that
          position to its opposite in the screen.
          
          'none' is an alias to 'simple' that also sets the 'transition-step' to 255. This has the
          effect of the transition finishing instantly
          
          'fade' is similar to 'simple' but the fade is controlled through the --transition-bezier
          flag
          
          'wipe' is similar to 'left' but allows you to specify the angle for transition with the
          `--transition-angle` flag.
          
          'wave' is similar to 'wipe' sweeping line is wavy
          
          'grow' causes a growing circle to transition across the screen and allows changing the
          circle's center position with the `--transition-pos` flag.
          
          'center' is an alias to 'grow' with position set to center of screen.
          
          'any' is an alias to 'grow' with position set to a random point on screen.
          
          'outer' is the same as grow but the circle shrinks instead of growing.
          
          Finally, 'random' will select a transition effect at random
          
          [env: SWWW_TRANSITION=]
          [default: simple]

      --transition-step <TRANSITION_STEP>
          How fast the transition approaches the new image.
          
          The transition logic works by adding or subtracting from the current rgb values until the
          old image transforms in the new one. This controls by how much we add or subtract.
          
          Larger values will make the transition faster, but more abrupt. A value of 255 will always
          switch to the new image immediately.
          
          This defaults to 2 when transition-type is 'simple', and 90 otherwise
          
          [env: SWWW_TRANSITION_STEP=]
          [default: 90]

      --transition-duration <TRANSITION_DURATION>
          How long the transition takes to complete in seconds.
          
          Note that this doesn't work with the 'simple' transition
          
          [env: SWWW_TRANSITION_DURATION=]
          [default: 3]

      --transition-fps <TRANSITION_FPS>
          Frame rate for the transition effect.
          
          Note there is no point in setting this to a value smaller than what your monitor supports.
          
          Also note this is **different** from the transition-step. That one controls by how much we
          approach the new image every frame.
          
          [env: SWWW_TRANSITION_FPS=]
          [default: 30]

      --transition-angle <TRANSITION_ANGLE>
          This is used for the 'wipe' and 'wave' transitions. It controls the angle of the wipe
          
          Note that the angle is in degrees, where '0' is right to left and '90' is top to bottom,
          and '270' bottom to top
          
          [env: SWWW_TRANSITION_ANGLE=]
          [default: 45]

      --transition-pos <TRANSITION_POS>
          This is only used for the 'grow','outer' transitions. It controls the center of circle
          (default is 'center').
          
          Position values can be given in both percentage values and pixel values: float values are
          interpreted as percentages and integer values as pixel values eg: 0.5,0.5 means 50% of the
          screen width and 50% of the screen height 200,400 means 200 pixels from the left and 400
          pixels from the bottom
          
          the value can also be an alias which will set the position accordingly): 'center' | 'top'
          | 'left' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'top-left' | 'top-right' | 'bottom-left' | 'bottom-right'
          
          [env: SWWW_TRANSITION_POS=]
          [default: center]

      --transition-bezier <TRANSITION_BEZIER>
          bezier curve to use for the transition https://cubic-bezier.com is a good website to get
          these values from
          
          eg: 0.0,0.0,1.0,1.0 for linear animation
          
          [env: SWWW_TRANSITION_BEZIER=]
          [default: .54,0,.34,.99]

      --transition-wave <TRANSITION_WAVE>
          currently only used for 'wave' transition to control the width and height of each wave
          
          [env: SWWW_TRANSITION_WAVE=]
          [default: 20,20]

      --invert-y
          inverts the y position sent in 'transition_pos' flag
          
          [env: INVERT_Y=]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

=== swww-daemon --help ===
swww-daemon

Options:

    -f|--format <argb|abgr|rgb|bgr>
        Force the use of a specific wl_shm format.

        By default, swww-daemon will use argb, because it is most widely
        supported. Generally speaking, formats with 3 channels will use 3/4 the
        memory of formats with 4 channels. Also, bgr formats are more efficient
        than rgb formats because we do not need to do an extra swap of the bytes
        when decoding the image (though the difference is unnoticiable).

    -l|--layer <background|bottom>
        Which layer to display the background in. Defaults to `background`.

        We do not accept layers `top` and `overlay` because those would make
        your desktop unusable by simply putting an image on top of everything
        else. If there is ever a use case for these, we can reconsider this.

=== awww --help ===
An Answer to your Wayland Wallpaper Woes

Change what your monitors display as a background by controlling the awww daemon at runtime.
Supports animated gifs and putting different stuff in different monitors. I also did my best to make
it as resource efficient as possible.

Note `awww` will only work in a compositor that implements the layer-shell protocol. Typically,
wlr-roots based compositors.

Usage: awww <COMMAND>

Commands:
  clear        Fills the specified outputs with the given color
  restore      Restores the last displayed image on the specified outputs
  clear-cache  Clears the awww cache
  img          Sends an image (or animated gif) for the daemon to display
  toggle       Toggles the daemon
  pause        Pauses the daemon
  unpause      Unpauses the daemon
  kill         Kills the daemon
  query        Asks the daemon to print output information (names and dimensions)
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

=== awww img --help (transition types) ===
  -t, --transition-type <TRANSITION_TYPE>
          Sets the type of transition. Default is 'simple', that fades into the new image
          
          Possible transitions are:
--
          This defaults to 2 when transition-type is 'simple', and 90 otherwise
          
          [env: AWWW_TRANSITION_STEP=]
          [default: 90]

=== awww-daemon --help ===
awww-daemon

Options:

    -f|--format <argb|abgr|rgb|bgr>
        Force the use of a specific wl_shm format.

        By default, awww-daemon will use argb, because it is most widely
        supported. Generally speaking, formats with 3 channels will use 3/4 the
        memory of formats with 4 channels. Also, bgr formats are more efficient
        than rgb formats because we do not need to do an extra swap of the bytes
        when decoding the image (though the difference is unnoticiable).

    -l|--layer <background|bottom>
        Which layer to display the background in. Defaults to `background`.

        We do not accept layers `top` and `overlay` because those would make
        your desktop unusable by simply putting an image on top of everything
        else. If there is ever a use case for these, we can reconsider this.


=== awww query --help ===
Asks the daemon to print output information (names and dimensions).

You may use this to find out valid values for the <awww-img --outputs> option. If you want more
detailed information about your outputs, I would recommend trying wlr-randr.

#!/bin/bash
# Applies the boot wallpaper once awww's IPC daemon is actually ready.
#
# awww (nixpkgs' current name for the swww project -- same author, same CLI,
# just renamed upstream) is started by Hyprland's autostart (see
# hyprland.lua) immediately before this script. Unlike the old yin daemon,
# awww doesn't expose a documented fixed socket path to poll, so readiness
# is checked the supported way: `awww query` fails until the daemon is
# actually listening.
#
# `awww img` with no --outputs applies to every output in one call, so unlike
# the old yinctl-based version this script no longer needs to enumerate
# monitors itself.

set -u

IMG="/home/krubics/.config/hypr/images/latios-latias.jpg"
LOG="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/hypr/wallpaper-autostart.log"

QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS=5000   # give up waiting for the daemon after ~5s
RETRIES=20              # then retry the apply loop this many times (0.1s apart)
POLL_MS=100

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"

log() {
    printf '%s [wallpaper-autostart] %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$1" >> "$LOG"
}

log "starting; waiting for awww to answer queries (timeout ${QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS}ms)"

#!/bin/bash
# Usage: set-wallpaper.sh /path/to/image-or-video [transition]
# Applies the wallpaper via awww (nixpkgs' current name for swww -- the
# project renamed itself upstream, same CLI shape). awww only ever renders
# still images and animated gifs, so video files (mp4/mkv/mov/webm) are
# played per-monitor with mpvpaper instead, same as before yin unified both
# under one daemon.

WALLPAPER="$1"
TRANSITION="$2"   # optional, e.g. wipe / grow (see `awww img --help` -> -t)
[ -z "$WALLPAPER" ] && { echo "Usage: $0 <path> [transition]"; exit 1; }

VIDEO_OPTS="no-audio loop hwdec=auto scale=bilinear interpolation=no video-sync=display-resample panscan=1.0 video-scale-x=1.0 video-scale-y=1.0 video-align-x=0.5 video-align-y=0.5 load-scripts=no"

is_video() {
    case "${1,,}" in
        *.mp4|*.mkv|*.mov|*.webm) return 0 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

# A new wallpaper -- of either kind -- always supersedes a running video one.
pkill -f -9 mpvpaper 2>/dev/null

if is_video "$WALLPAPER"; then
    monitors=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[].name')
    if [ -z "$monitors" ]; then
        mpvpaper -o "$VIDEO_OPTS" '*' "$WALLPAPER" &
    else
        while IFS= read -r m; do
            [ -z "$m" ] && continue
            mpvpaper -o "$VIDEO_OPTS" "$m" "$WALLPAPER" &
        done <<< "$monitors"
    fi
    # mpvpaper has no transition concept -- $TRANSITION is intentionally unused here.
else
    trans_args=()
    [ -n "$TRANSITION" ] && trans_args=(--transition-type "$TRANSITION")
    # No --outputs: applies to every monitor in a single IPC call.
    awww img "$WALLPAPER" "${trans_args[@]}"
fi

# Regenerate the colour scheme for this wallpaper. Use an absolute path so this
# works regardless of the caller's working directory (e.g. a Hyprland keybind).
# Videos ship a pre-baked matugen JSON (matugen can't sample a video frame);
# images without one derive their palette live from the file.
wp_file="${WALLPAPER##*/}"
wp_stem="${wp_file%%.*}"
colors_json="$HOME/.config/hypr/matugen-colors/$wp_stem.json"
if [ -f "$colors_json" ]; then
  matugen json "$colors_json"
elif [ -f "$WALLPAPER" ] && file --mime-type -b "$WALLPAPER" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^image/'; then
  matugen image "$WALLPAPER"
else
  echo "set-wallpaper: no matugen palette for '$wp_stem' and '$WALLPAPER' is not an image; skipping colours" >&2
fi


# Track current wallpaper for restarts
ln -sf "$WALLPAPER" ~/.cache/current-wallpaper

This is really just an artifact of testing through the bash tool, which spawns a shell, runs the command, and exits. In actual production, the script gets invoked directly by Hyprland's dispatcher or through rofi keybinds, where Hyprland handles the process spawning and detachment properly — the script isn't tied to a parent shell that would kill its children. The original reference script does the same thing (backgrounding mpvpaper with `&`), but it works because it's being executed as a foreground async invocation from Hyprland's dispatcher, not wrapped in a shell that exits.

#!/bin/bash
# Applies the boot wallpaper once awww's IPC daemon is actually ready.
#
# awww (nixpkgs' current name for the swww project -- same author, same CLI,
# just renamed upstream) is started by Hyprland's autostart (see
# hyprland.lua) immediately before this script. Unlike the old yin daemon,
# awww doesn't expose a documented fixed socket path to poll, so readiness
# is checked the supported way: `awww query` fails until the daemon is
# actually listening.
#
# `awww img` with no --outputs applies to every output in one call, so unlike
# the old yinctl-based version this script no longer needs to enumerate
# monitors itself.

set -u

IMG="/home/krubics/.config/hypr/images/latios-latias.jpg"
LOG="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/hypr/wallpaper-autostart.log"

QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS=5000   # give up waiting for the daemon after ~5s
RETRIES=20              # then retry the apply loop this many times (0.1s apart)
POLL_MS=100

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"

log() {
    printf '%s [wallpaper-autostart] %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$1" >> "$LOG"
}

log "starting; waiting for awww to answer queries (timeout ${QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS}ms)"

# 1. Wait for awww-daemon to come up and start answering IPC queries.
waited=0
until awww query >/dev/null 2>&1; do
    if [ "$waited" -ge "$QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS" ]; then
        log "ERROR: awww did not become ready within ${QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS}ms; aborting"
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 0.1
    waited=$((waited + POLL_MS))
done
log "awww ready after ${waited}ms"

# 2. Apply the wallpaper to every output, retrying until it succeeds.
attempt=1
while :; do
    if awww img "$IMG" >> "$LOG" 2>&1; then
        log "wallpaper applied on attempt ${attempt} (img=$IMG)"
        exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -ge "$RETRIES" ]; then
        log "ERROR: wallpaper apply failed after ${attempt} attempts"
        exit 1
    fi
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Usage: set-wallpaper.lua /path/to/image-or-video [transition]
--
-- Applies the wallpaper via awww (nixpkgs' current name for swww -- the
-- project renamed itself upstream, same CLI shape). awww only ever renders
-- still images and animated gifs, so video files (.mp4/.mkv/.mov/.webm) are
-- played per-monitor with mpvpaper instead.
--
-- The transition is looked up in conf/wallpapers.lua by filename when not
-- passed explicitly as $2 -- edit that file to change per-wallpaper
-- transitions.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers_conf = require("conf.wallpapers")

local wallpaper = arg[1]
local transition = arg[2]

if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
    io.stderr:write("Usage: set-wallpaper.lua <path> [transition]\n")
    os.exit(1)
end

local VIDEO_OPTS = "no-audio loop hwdec=auto scale=bilinear interpolation=no "
    .. "video-sync=display-resample panscan=1.0 video-scale-x=1.0 "
    .. "video-scale-y=1.0 video-align-x=0.5 video-align-y=0.5 load-scripts=no"

local function shell_quote(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
    if type(ok) == "number" then
        return ok == 0
    end
    return ok == true
end

local function is_video(path)
    local ext = path:match("%.([%w]+)$")
    if not ext then
        return false
    end
    ext = ext:lower()
    return ext == "mp4" or ext == "mkv" or ext == "mov" or ext == "webm"
end

local function file_exists(path)
    local f = io.open(path, "r")
    if f then
        f:close()
        return true
    end
    return false
end

local function is_image(path)
    local p = io.popen("file --mime-type -b " .. shell_quote(path) .. " 2>/dev/null")
    if not p then
        return false
    end
    local mime = p:read("*l") or ""
    p:close()
    return mime:match("^image/") ~= nil
end

if not transition or transition == "" then
    transition = wallpapers_conf.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers_conf.default_transition
end

-- A new wallpaper -- of either kind -- always supersedes a running video one.
os.execute("pkill -f -9 mpvpaper 2>/dev/null")

if is_video(wallpaper) then
    local monitors = {}
    local p = io.popen("hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[].name' 2>/dev/null")
    if p then
        for line in p:lines() do
            if line ~= "" then
                table.insert(monitors, line)
            end
        end
        p:close()
    end

    if #monitors == 0 then
        os.execute(string.format("mpvpaper -o %s '*' %s &", shell_quote(VIDEO_OPTS), shell_quote(wallpaper)))
    else
        for _, m in ipairs(monitors) do
            os.execute(string.format("mpvpaper -o %s %s %s &", shell_quote(VIDEO_OPTS), shell_quote(m), shell_quote(wallpaper)))
        end
    end
    -- mpvpaper has no transition concept -- `transition` is intentionally unused here.
else
    local trans_arg = ""
    if transition and transition ~= "" then
        trans_arg = " --transition-type " .. shell_quote(transition)
    end
    exec_ok("awww img " .. shell_quote(wallpaper) .. trans_arg)
end

-- Regenerate the colour scheme for this wallpaper. Videos ship a pre-baked
-- matugen JSON (matugen can't sample a video frame); images without one
-- derive their palette live from the file.
local wp_file = basename(wallpaper)
local wp_stem = wp_file:match("^([^.]+)") or wp_file
local colors_json = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/matugen-colors/" .. wp_stem .. ".json"

if file_exists(colors_json) then
    os.execute("matugen json " .. shell_quote(colors_json))
elseif file_exists(wallpaper) and is_image(wallpaper) then
    os.execute("matugen image " .. shell_quote(wallpaper))
else
    io.stderr:write(string.format(
        "set-wallpaper: no matugen palette for '%s' and '%s' is not an image; skipping colours\n",
        wp_stem, wallpaper
    ))
end

-- Track current wallpaper for restarts
os.execute("ln -sf " .. shell_quote(wallpaper) .. " " .. shell_quote(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper"))

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Applies the boot wallpaper once awww's IPC daemon is actually ready.
--
-- awww (nixpkgs' current name for the swww project -- same author, same CLI,
-- just renamed upstream) is started by Hyprland's autostart (see
-- hyprland.lua) immediately before this script. awww doesn't expose a
-- documented fixed socket path to poll, so readiness is checked the
-- supported way: `awww query` fails until the daemon is actually listening.
--
-- `awww img` with no --outputs applies to every output in one call, so this
-- script doesn't need to enumerate monitors itself.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
local IMG = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/wallpapers/latios-latias.png"
local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-autostart.log"

local QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 -- give up waiting for the daemon after ~5s
local RETRIES = 20            -- then retry the apply loop this many times (0.1s apart)
local POLL_MS = 100

local function shell_quote(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
    if type(ok) == "number" then
        return ok == 0
    end
    return ok == true
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. shell_quote(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-autostart] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function sleep_ms(ms)
    os.execute("sleep " .. (ms / 1000))
end

log(string.format("starting; waiting for awww to answer queries (timeout %dms)", QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS))

-- 1. Wait for awww-daemon to come up and start answering IPC queries.
local waited = 0
while not exec_ok("awww query >/dev/null 2>&1") do
    if waited >= QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS then
        log(string.format("ERROR: awww did not become ready within %dms; aborting", QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS))
        os.exit(1)
    end
    sleep_ms(POLL_MS)
    waited = waited + POLL_MS
end
log(string.format("awww ready after %dms", waited))

-- 2. Apply the wallpaper to every output, retrying until it succeeds.
local attempt = 1
while true do
    if exec_ok("awww img " .. shell_quote(IMG) .. " >> " .. shell_quote(LOG) .. " 2>&1") then
        log(string.format("wallpaper applied on attempt %d (img=%s)", attempt, IMG))
        os.exit(0)
    end
    if attempt >= RETRIES then
        log(string.format("ERROR: wallpaper apply failed after %d attempts", attempt))
        os.exit(1)
    end
    attempt = attempt + 1
    sleep_ms(POLL_MS)
end

-- Wallpaper picker: lists files under ~/.config/hypr/wallpapers via rofi,
-- then applies the pick through set-wallpaper.lua. Per-wallpaper transitions
-- are configured in conf/wallpapers.lua, not here.

local ROFI_THEME = HOME .. "/.config/rofi/launchers/type-1/style-6.rasi"
local SET_WALLPAPER = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/scripts/set-wallpaper.lua"

local function shell_quote(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

    "find %s -type f | rofi -dmenu -i -p 'Wallpaper' -theme %s",
    shell_quote(WALLPAPER_DIR), shell_quote(ROFI_THEME)
)

local p = io.popen(pick_cmd)
local pick = p and p:read("*l") or nil
if p then
    p:close()
end

if not pick or pick == "" then
    os.exit(0)
end

os.execute(SET_WALLPAPER .. " " .. shell_quote(pick))

--  runs the old-style dispatcher string verbatim — it's the bridge

local modKey = "SUPER"

-- ============================================================
--  APPLICATIONS  (SUPER + SHIFT = launch)

hl.bind(modKey .. " + SPACE",          hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.launcher))
-- hl.bind(modKey .. " + B",      hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.browser))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + F",          hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.yazi))   -- yazi (terminal FM)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + SHIFT + F",  hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.files))  -- nautilus (moved off SUPER+SHIFT+F for herdr search)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + O",      hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.obsidian))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + A",      function()
  hl.exec_cmd(vars.browser)
  hl.exec_cmd(vars.terminal)
end)

---- Scroll -------------------------------------------------------
-- hl.bind("ALT + semicolon", hl.dsp.scroll({ direction = "down" }))
hl.bind("ALT + P", function() 
  hl.exec_cmd("move +col")
end)

-- ============================================================
--  WINDOW MANAGEMENT  (SUPER)
-- ============================================================
hl.bind(modKey .. " + Q", hl.dsp.window.close())                     -- close window
hl.bind(modKey .. " + D", hl.dsp.window.float({ action = "toggle" })) -- toggle float
hl.bind(modKey .. " + J", hl.dsp.exec_raw("togglesplit"))            -- flip split axis
hl.bind(modKey .. " + bracketright", hl.dsp.window.fullscreen({ mode = 0 }))    -- fullscreen
hl.bind(modKey .. " + GRAVE", hl.dsp.layout("rotatesplit 90"))
-- (0.55 quirk: fullscreen toggle-off can misfire from a bind; works via hyprctl)

-- Pop out: float + size + center + pin  (Omarchy's SUPER+O)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + O", function()
  hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.float({ action = "set" }))
  hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_raw("resizeactive exact 50% 50%"))
  hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_raw("centerwindow"))
  hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_raw("pin"))
end)

-- Toggle whole-workspace layout dwindle <-> master  (Omarchy's SUPER+L)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + N", function()
  if hl.get_config("general.layout") == "dwindle" then
    hl.config({ general = { layout = "master" } })
    hl.exec_cmd("notify-send Layout Master -t 3000")
  else
    hl.config({ general = { layout = "dwindle" } })
    hl.exec_cmd("notify-send Layout Dwindle -t 3000")
  end
end)

-- ---- Focus / swap / cycle ----------------------------------
hl.bind(modKey  .. " + L",  hl.dsp.focus({ direction = "l" }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + apostrophe", hl.dsp.focus({ direction = "r" }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + P",    hl.dsp.focus({ direction = "u" }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + semicolon",  hl.dsp.focus({ direction = "d" }))


-- ---- Resize (horizontal, Omarchy default) ------------------
hl.bind(modKey .. " + minus", hl.dsp.window.resize({ x = 100*(16/9), y = 100, relative = true }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + equal", hl.dsp.window.resize({ x = -100*(16/9), y = -100, relative = true }))

-- ---- Mouse move / resize -----------------------------------
hl.bind(modKey .. " + mouse:272", hl.dsp.window.drag(),   { mouse = true })
hl.bind(modKey .. " + mouse:273", hl.dsp.window.resize(), { mouse = true })

-- ============================================================
--  WORKSPACES  (SUPER = go, +SHIFT = move, +SHIFT+ALT = silent)
-- ============================================================
for i = 1, 9 do
    hl.bind(modKey .. " + " .. i, hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = i }))
    hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + " .. i, hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = i }))
    hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + ALT + " .. i, hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = i, silent = true }))
end

hl.bind(modKey .. " + ALT + 0", hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = 10 }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + ALT + 0", hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = 10, silent = true }))

for name, trans in pairs(wallpaper_transitions) do

hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + Space", hl.dsp.exec_cmd(string.format([[
pick="$(find ~/.config/hypr/wallpapers -type f | rofi -dmenu -i -p 'Wallpaper' -theme ~/.config/rofi/launchers/type-1/style-6.rasi)"
[ -z "$pick" ] && exit 0

hl.bind(modKey .. " + ALT + D", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("/home/krubics/.local/share/hyprwhspr/src/config/hyprland/hyprwhspr-tray.sh record"))

-- ============================================================
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + S",   hl.dsp.exec_cmd("hyprshot -m region"))

-- hyprland.lua) immediately before this script. awww doesn't expose a
-- documented fixed socket path to poll, so readiness is checked the
-- supported way: `awww query` fails until the daemon is actually listening.
--
-- `awww img` with no --outputs applies to every output in one call, so this
-- script doesn't need to enumerate monitors itself.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
local IMG = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/wallpapers/latios-latias.png"
local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-autostart.log"

local QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 -- give up waiting for the daemon after ~5s
local RETRIES = 20            -- then retry the apply loop this many times (0.1s apart)
local POLL_MS = 100

local function shell_quote(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
    if type(ok) == "number" then
        return ok == 0
    end
    return ok == true
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. shell_quote(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-autostart] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function sleep_ms(ms)
    os.execute("sleep " .. (ms / 1000))
end

log(string.format("starting; waiting for awww to answer queries (timeout %dms)", QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS))

-- 1. Wait for awww-daemon to come up and start answering IPC queries.
local waited = 0
while not exec_ok("awww query >/dev/null 2>&1") do
    if waited >= QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS then
        log(string.format("ERROR: awww did not become ready within %dms; aborting", QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS))
        os.exit(1)
    end
    sleep_ms(POLL_MS)
    waited = waited + POLL_MS
end
log(string.format("awww ready after %dms", waited))

-- 2. Apply the wallpaper to every output, retrying until it succeeds.
local attempt = 1
while true do
    if exec_ok("awww img " .. shell_quote(IMG) .. " >> " .. shell_quote(LOG) .. " 2>&1") then
        log(string.format("wallpaper applied on attempt %d (img=%s)", attempt, IMG))
        os.exit(0)
    end
    if attempt >= RETRIES then
        log(string.format("ERROR: wallpaper apply failed after %d attempts", attempt))
        os.exit(1)
    end
    attempt = attempt + 1
    sleep_ms(POLL_MS)
end

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Usage: set-wallpaper.lua /path/to/image-or-video [transition]
--
-- Applies the wallpaper via awww (nixpkgs' current name for swww -- the
-- project renamed itself upstream, same CLI shape). awww only ever renders
-- still images and animated gifs, so video files (.mp4/.mkv/.mov/.webm) are
-- played per-monitor with mpvpaper instead.
--
-- The transition is looked up in conf/wallpapers.lua by filename when not
-- passed explicitly as $2 -- edit that file to change per-wallpaper
-- transitions.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers_conf = require("conf.wallpapers")

local wallpaper = arg[1]
local transition = arg[2]

if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
    io.stderr:write("Usage: set-wallpaper.lua <path> [transition]\n")
    os.exit(1)
end

local VIDEO_OPTS = "no-audio loop hwdec=auto scale=bilinear interpolation=no "
    .. "video-sync=display-resample panscan=1.0 video-scale-x=1.0 "
    .. "video-scale-y=1.0 video-align-x=0.5 video-align-y=0.5 load-scripts=no"

local function shell_quote(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
    if type(ok) == "number" then
        return ok == 0
    end
    return ok == true
end

local function is_video(path)
    local ext = path:match("%.([%w]+)$")
    if not ext then
        return false
    end
    ext = ext:lower()
    return ext == "mp4" or ext == "mkv" or ext == "mov" or ext == "webm"
end

local function file_exists(path)
    local f = io.open(path, "r")
    if f then
        f:close()
        return true
    end
    return false
end

local function is_image(path)
    local p = io.popen("file --mime-type -b " .. shell_quote(path) .. " 2>/dev/null")
    if not p then
        return false
    end
    local mime = p:read("*l") or ""
    p:close()
    return mime:match("^image/") ~= nil
end

if not transition or transition == "" then
    transition = wallpapers_conf.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers_conf.default_transition
end

-- A new wallpaper -- of either kind -- always supersedes a running video one.
os.execute("pkill -f -9 mpvpaper 2>/dev/null")

if is_video(wallpaper) then
    local monitors = {}
    local p = io.popen("hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[].name' 2>/dev/null")
    if p then
        for line in p:lines() do
            if line ~= "" then
                table.insert(monitors, line)
            end
        end
        p:close()
    end

    if #monitors == 0 then
        os.execute(string.format("mpvpaper -o %s '*' %s &", shell_quote(VIDEO_OPTS), shell_quote(wallpaper)))
    else
        for _, m in ipairs(monitors) do
            os.execute(string.format("mpvpaper -o %s %s %s &", shell_quote(VIDEO_OPTS), shell_quote(m), shell_quote(wallpaper)))
        end
    end
    -- mpvpaper has no transition concept -- `transition` is intentionally unused here.
else
    local trans_arg = ""
    if transition and transition ~= "" then
        trans_arg = " --transition-type " .. shell_quote(transition)
    end
    exec_ok("awww img " .. shell_quote(wallpaper) .. trans_arg)
end

-- Regenerate the colour scheme for this wallpaper. Videos ship a pre-baked
-- matugen JSON (matugen can't sample a video frame); images without one
-- derive their palette live from the file.
local wp_file = basename(wallpaper)
local wp_stem = wp_file:match("^([^.]+)") or wp_file
local colors_json = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/matugen-colors/" .. wp_stem .. ".json"

if file_exists(colors_json) then
    os.execute("matugen json " .. shell_quote(colors_json))
elseif file_exists(wallpaper) and is_image(wallpaper) then
    os.execute("matugen image " .. shell_quote(wallpaper))
else
    io.stderr:write(string.format(
        "set-wallpaper: no matugen palette for '%s' and '%s' is not an image; skipping colours\n",
        wp_stem, wallpaper
    ))
end

-- Track current wallpaper for restarts
os.execute("ln -sf " .. shell_quote(wallpaper) .. " " .. shell_quote(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper"))

        "set-wallpaper: no matugen palette for '%s' and '%s' is not an image; skipping colours\n",

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Applies the boot wallpaper once awww's IPC daemon is actually ready.
--
-- awww (nixpkgs' current name for the swww project -- same author, same CLI,
-- just renamed upstream) is started by Hyprland's autostart (see
-- hyprland.lua) immediately before this script. awww doesn't expose a
-- documented fixed socket path to poll, so readiness is checked the
-- supported way: `awww query` fails until the daemon is actually listening.
--
-- `awww img` with no --outputs applies to every output in one call, so this
-- script doesn't need to enumerate monitors itself.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
local IMG = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/wallpapers/latios-latias.png"
local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-autostart.log"

local QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 -- give up waiting for the daemon after ~5s
local RETRIES = 20            -- then retry the apply loop this many times (0.1s apart)
local POLL_MS = 100

local function shell_quote(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
    if type(ok) == "number" then
        return ok == 0
    end
    return ok == true
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. shell_quote(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-autostart] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function sleep_ms(ms)
    os.execute("sleep " .. (ms / 1000))
end

log(string.format("starting; waiting for awww to answer queries (timeout %dms)", QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS))

hl.on("hyprland.start", function()
    -- Start the awww wallpaper daemon first (nixpkgs' `swww` package was
    -- renamed upstream to `awww`; same project, same CLI shape). Absolute
    -- path: Hyprland's own process PATH predates home-manager installing
    -- this into ~/.nix-profile/bin, so a bare "awww-daemon" silently
    -- fails to launch (command not found) when dispatched from here.
    hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_cmd("/home/krubics/.nix-profile/bin/awww-daemon"))

    -- periodically so the next Hyprland start can restore again.

    hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_cmd("waybar"))

Looking at the frame-by-frame breakdown, I can see the latios-latias flash is still appearing at the 0.3-second mark between the old gojo video and the new one, which means my reordering approach didn't fully eliminate it.

The issue is that I'm spawning the new mpvpaper first, waiting 0.3 seconds for it to initialize, then killing the old process. But that 0.3-second window is exactly when both instances could be visible if the new one hasn't actually rendered its first frame yet—the spawn command starts, but the actual decode and frame rendering might take longer than the initialization sleep, especially under system contention. So at that precise moment when the old process dies, the new one still hasn't produced a visible frame, leaving a gap where the background layer shows through.

The real problem is that killing the old surface is synchronous and immediate, while the new mpvpaper reaching "first frame rendered" is asynchronous and unpredictable. My fixed sleep is just a guess that doesn't account for GPU contention or decode latency. A better approach would be event-driven—actually wait for the new instance to produce output (like checking its logs for rendering signals) rather than relying on a fixed timing guess.

But given how badly this test environment is struggling with frame drops across all my video tests (likely from GPU contention with grim screenshotting or just an overloaded system), even a generous fixed sleep like 0.6-1s might not be enough. I could increase the buffer as a pragmatic workaround to trade some extra latency for reliability, though that's really just masking the underlying race condition rather than fixing it properly.

The real question is whether there's a better approach than blind timing. Polling `hyprctl clients` won't help since layer-shell surfaces typically don't show up as regular clients. I could check CPU usage or process status files, but the simplest robust solution is probably just bumping the grace period to 0.8-1.0 seconds — based on my test observations, even under load the first frame usually renders within 100-300ms, so that should cover virtually all cases while keeping latency reasonable.

Actually, a cleaner approach might be to spawn the new instances and watch for when each one actually maps a surface before killing the old ones, but given the scope of this wallpaper picker script and the fact that mpvpaper doesn't expose an easy ready hook, a generous fixed delay is the pragmatic, industry-standard solution that most real-world tools use anyway.

Looking back at my earlier test data, the VO output typically appeared within the first 100ms, but under concurrent load with both old and new videos decoding simultaneously, it clearly needed more than 300ms. I'll bump the delay to 1.0 second and verify it works with the same rapid-screenshot method to ensure no glitches occur.

Actually, a much more robust approach would be to poll the new mpvpaper's stdout directly for the "VO:" marker instead of guessing a sleep duration — that's a reliable signal that video decoding has started and frames are being rendered. I could redirect each new mpvpaper instance's output to a temp file and watch for that marker with a reasonable timeout fallback (around 2 seconds max) before killing the old process. The IPC call blocks until the daemon acknowledges receipt, but the actual rendering and transition animation could still be in progress on the daemon's side—though the surface should already be committed and displaying something correct even if mid-transition.

    end
    return pids
end

if is_video(wallpaper) then
    -- Start the new video first (it maps its own layer-shell surface on top
    -- of whatever is currently showing), *then* kill only the previously-
    -- running instances -- never the ones just spawned.
    local old_pids = mpvpaper_pids()

    local monitors = {}
    local p = io.popen("hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[].name' 2>/dev/null")
    if p then
        for line in p:lines() do
            if line ~= "" then
                table.insert(monitors, line)
            end
        end
        p:close()
    end

    -- Redirect each new instance's own output to a log file so readiness
    -- can be detected by evidence (mpv prints "VO:" once it has actually
    -- set up video output and is about to render), not a guessed delay --
    -- under GPU/decode contention with the outgoing video, a fixed sleep
    -- proved too short and still let the awww layer flash through.
    local logfiles = {}
    local function spawn(monitor)
        local logfile = os.tmpname()
        table.insert(logfiles, logfile)
        os.execute(string.format(
            "mpvpaper -o %s %s %s > %s 2>&1 &",
            shell_quote(VIDEO_OPTS), shell_quote(monitor), shell_quote(wallpaper), shell_quote(logfile)
        ))
    end

    if #monitors == 0 then
        spawn("*")
    else
        for _, m in ipairs(monitors) do
            spawn(m)
        end
    end
    -- mpvpaper has no transition concept -- `transition` is intentionally unused here.

    if #old_pids > 0 then
        local READY_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000
        local POLL_MS = 50
        local waited = 0
        while waited < READY_TIMEOUT_MS do
            local all_ready = true
            for _, lf in ipairs(logfiles) do
                local f = io.open(lf, "r")
                local content = f and f:read("*a") or ""
                if f then f:close() end
                if not content:find("VO:") then
                    all_ready = false
                    break
                end
            end
            if all_ready then break end
            os.execute("sleep 0.05")
            waited = waited + POLL_MS
        end
        for _, pid in ipairs(old_pids) do
            os.execute("kill -9 " .. pid .. " 2>/dev/null")
        end
    end

    for _, lf in ipairs(logfiles) do
        os.remove(lf)
    end
else
    -- Set the new image on awww's layer first -- invisible for now if a video
    -- is still covering it -- then remove the video, which reveals the
    -- already-correct new image instead of whatever was cached before it.
    local trans_arg = ""
    if transition and transition ~= "" then
        trans_arg = " --transition-type " .. shell_quote(transition)
    end
    exec_ok(shell_quote(AWWW) .. " img " .. shell_quote(wallpaper) .. trans_arg)
    os.execute("pkill -f -9 mpvpaper 2>/dev/null")
end

-- Regenerate the colour scheme for this wallpaper. Videos ship a pre-baked
-- matugen JSON (matugen can't sample a video frame); images without one
-- derive their palette live from the file.
local wp_file = basename(wallpaper)
local wp_stem = wp_file:match("^([^.]+)") or wp_file
local colors_json = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/matugen-colors/" .. wp_stem .. ".json"

if file_exists(colors_json) then
    os.execute("matugen json " .. shell_quote(colors_json))
elseif file_exists(wallpaper) and is_image(wallpaper) then
    os.execute("matugen image " .. shell_quote(wallpaper))
else
    io.stderr:write(string.format(
        "set-wallpaper: no matugen palette for '%s' and '%s' is not an image; skipping colours\n",
        wp_stem, wallpaper
    ))
end

-- Track current wallpaper for restarts
os.execute("ln -sf " .. shell_quote(wallpaper) .. " " .. shell_quote(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper"))

protocol**. ## Build ### Dependencies: - wayland-client and wayland-protocol `.xml` files installed in your system (`pkg-config` must be able to find it) - Up to date stable rustc compiler and cargo (specifically, MSRV is 1.87.0) To build, clone this repository and run: ``` cargo build --release ``` Then, put **both binaries** `target/release/swww` and `target/release/swww-daemon` in your path. Optionally, autocompletion scripts for bash, zsh, fish and elvish are offered in the `completions` directory. #### Man pages: In order to generate the man pages, **you must have `scdoc` installed**. Run ``` ./doc/gen.sh ``` The man pages will be in `doc/generated`. To install them, you must move them to to the appropriate location in your system. You should be able to figure out where that is by running `manpath`. ### Nix NixOS users can directly use this repository to get the latest swww for their system. Add in your `flake.nix`: ```nix inputs.swww.url = "github:LGFae/swww"; ``` Pass inputs to your modules using `specialArgs` and Then in `configuration.nix`: ```nix environment.systemPackages = [ inputs.swww.packages.${pkgs.system}.swww ]; ``` ## Features - Display animated gifs on your desktop - Display any image in the formats: * avif (note: must have `dav1d` dependency and compile with `--features=avif` flag) * jpeg * png * gif * pnm * tga * tiff * webp * bmp * farbfeld * svg (only static svgs are supported) - Clear the screen with an arbitrary rrggbb color - Smooth transition effect when you switch images - Do all of that without having to shutdown and reinitialize the daemon ## Why There are two main reasons that compelled me to make this: the first is that [`oguri`](https://github.com/vilhalmer/oguri) is unmaintained and archived, despite there being serious problems with excess of memory use while displaying certain gifs (see [this](https://github.com/vilhalmer/oguri/issues/38), for example). The best alternative I've found for `oguri` was [`mpvpaper`](https://github.com/GhostNaN/mpvpaper), but if felt overkill for my purposes. Comparing to `oguri`, `swww` uses less cpu power to animate once it has cached all the frames in the animation. It should also be **significantly** more memory efficient. The second is that, to my knowledge, there is no wallpaper daemon for wayland that allows you to change the wallpaper at runtime. That is, in order to, for example, cycle through the images of a directory, you'd have to kill the daemon and restart it. Not only does it make simple shell scripts a pain to write, it makes switching from one image to the next to happen very abruptly. ## Usage Start by initializing the daemon: ``` swww-daemon ``` Then, in a different terminal, simply pass the image you want to display: ``` swww img # You can also specify outputs: swww img -o # Control how smoothly the transition will happen, as well as its frame rate. # --transition-step: smaller values = smoother. Default is 2 if --transition-type is `simple`, and 90 if it is not. # --transition-fps: Default = 30. swww img --transition-step <1 to 255> --transition-fps <1 to 255> # There are also many different transition effects: swww img --transition-type center # Note you may also control the above by setting up the SWWW_TRANSITION_FPS, # SWWW_TRANSITION_STEP, and SWWW_TRANSITION environment variables. # To see all options, run swww img --help ``` If you would like to know the valid values for *\*, you can query the daemon. This will also tell you what the current image being displayed is, as well as the dimensions detected for the outputs. If you need more detailed information, I would recommend using [`wlr-randr`](https://sr.ht/~emersion/wlr-randr/). ``` swww query ``` Finally, to stop the daemon, kill it: ``` swww kill ``` For a more complete description, run `swww --help` or `swww --help`. Finally, to get a feel for what you can do with some shell scripting, check out the [example_scripts](/example_scripts/) folder. It can help you get started. ## Transitions #### Example wipe transition: > wipe transition with angle set to 30 deg ![top transition demonstration](../demos/assets/wipe.gif) The `left`, `right`, `top` and `bottom` transitions all work similarly. #### Example outer transition ![outer transition demonstration](../demos/assets/outer.gif) The `center` transition is the opposite: it starts from the center and goes towards the edges. There is also `simple`, which simply fades into the new image, `any`, which starts at a random point with either `center` of `outer` transitions, and `random`, which selects a transition effect at random. ## Troubleshooting ### High cpu usage during caching of a gif's frames `swww` will use a non-insignificant amount of cpu power while caching the images. This will be specially noticeable if the images need to be resized before being displayed. So, if you have a very large gif, I would recommend resizing it **before** sending it to `swww`. #!/bin/sh
# For each display, changes the wallpaper to a randomly chosen image in
# a given directory at a set interval.

DEFAULT_INTERVAL=300 # In seconds

if [ $# -lt 1 ] || [ ! -d "$1" ]; then
	printf "Usage:\n\t\e[1m%s\e[0m \e[4mDIRECTORY\e[0m [\e[4mINTERVAL\e[0m]\n" "$0"
	printf "\tChanges the wallpaper to a randomly chosen image in DIRECTORY every\n\tINTERVAL seconds (or every %d seconds if unspecified)." "$DEFAULT_INTERVAL"
	exit 1
fi

# See swww-img(1)
RESIZE_TYPE="fit"
export SWWW_TRANSITION_FPS="${SWWW_TRANSITION_FPS:-60}"
export SWWW_TRANSITION_STEP="${SWWW_TRANSITION_STEP:-2}"

while true; do
	find "$1" -type f \
	| while read -r img; do
		echo "$(</dev/urandom tr -dc a-zA-Z0-9 | head -c 8):$img"
	done \
	| sort -n | cut -d':' -f2- \
	| while read -r img; do
		for d in $(swww query | awk '{print $2}' | sed s/://); do # see swww-query(1)
			# Get next random image for this display, or re-shuffle images
			# and pick again if no more unused images are remaining
			[ -z "$img" ] && if read -r img; then true; else break 2; fi
			swww img --resize "$RESIZE_TYPE" --outputs "$d" "$img"
			unset -v img # Each image should only be used once per loop
		done
		sleep "${2:-$DEFAULT_INTERVAL}"
	done
done

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Usage: set-wallpaper.lua <path> [transition]
-- Images go through awww (nixpkgs' current name for swww, renamed upstream).
-- Videos (.mp4/.mkv/.mov/.webm) go through mpvpaper instead, since awww only
-- renders stills/gifs. Transition is looked up in conf/wallpapers.lua when
-- not passed explicitly.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
local AWWW = HOME .. "/.nix-profile/bin/awww" -- not on Hyprland's own PATH
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local wallpaper = arg[1]
local transition = arg[2]
if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
    io.stderr:write("Usage: set-wallpaper.lua <path> [transition]\n")
    os.exit(1)
end

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

local function each_line(cmd)
    local p = io.popen(cmd)
    return function()
        if not p then return nil end
        local line = p:read("*l")
        if not line then p:close(); p = nil end
        return line
    end
end

local video_exts = { mp4 = true, mkv = true, mov = true, webm = true }
local ext = wallpaper:match("%.(%w+)$")
local is_video = ext and video_exts[ext:lower()]

if not transition or transition == "" then
    transition = wallpapers.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers.default_transition
end

if is_video then
    -- Start the new video *before* killing the old one: awww's own layer
    -- keeps whatever was last set on it underneath, so killing mpvpaper
    -- first flashes through to that (usually unrelated) image.
    local old_pids = {}
    for pid in each_line("pgrep -f mpvpaper") do table.insert(old_pids, pid) end

    local opts = "no-audio loop hwdec=auto scale=bilinear video-sync=display-resample panscan=1.0 load-scripts=no"
    local monitors = {}
    for m in each_line("hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[].name' 2>/dev/null") do table.insert(monitors, m) end
    if #monitors == 0 then monitors = { "*" } end
    for _, m in ipairs(monitors) do
        os.execute(("mpvpaper -o %s %s %s &"):format(sh(opts), sh(m), sh(wallpaper)))
    end

    if #old_pids > 0 then
        os.execute("sleep 0.5") -- give the new instance(s) time to map before old ones die
        for _, pid in ipairs(old_pids) do
            os.execute("kill -9 " .. pid .. " 2>/dev/null")
        end
    end
else
    os.execute(("%s img %s --transition-type %s"):format(sh(AWWW), sh(wallpaper), sh(transition)))
    os.execute("pkill -9 -f mpvpaper 2>/dev/null")
end

-- Regenerate matugen colours: prefer a pre-baked JSON (videos ship one,
-- since matugen can't sample a video frame), else derive live from the image.
local stem = basename(wallpaper):match("^([^.]+)") or wallpaper
local colors_json = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/matugen-colors/" .. stem .. ".json"
local f = io.open(colors_json, "r")
if f then
    f:close()
    os.execute("matugen json " .. sh(colors_json))
elseif not is_video then
    os.execute("matugen image " .. sh(wallpaper))
end

os.execute("ln -sf " .. sh(wallpaper) .. " " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper"))

# mpvpaper
### mpvpaper is a wallpaper program for wlroots based wayland compositors, such as sway. That allows you to play videos with mpv as your wallpaper.

## Dependencies
- [mpv](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv)
- [wlroots](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wlroots/wlroots)

## Building 
### Building Requirements:

- ninja
- meson
- libmpv
### Clone | Build | Install:
```
# Clone
git clone --single-branch https://github.com/GhostNaN/mpvpaper
# Build
cd mpvpaper
meson setup build --prefix=/usr/local
ninja -C build
# Install
ninja -C build install
```
## Usage
Simple example:
```
mpvpaper DP-2 /path/to/video
```
To play the same video on all outputs:
```
mpvpaper ALL /path/to/video
```
You can also forward mpv options by passing "--mpv-options" or "-o" like so:
```
mpvpaper -o "no-audio --loop-playlist shuffle" HDMI-A-1 www.url/to/playlist
```
You can also control mpvpaper just like mpv in the terminal with keyboard bindings. 

But if you would like to  control mpvpaper while it's forked, you could use a mpv input-ipc-server like this:
```
mpvpaper -o "input-ipc-server=/tmp/mpv-socket" DP-1 /path/to/video
```
Then input commands with socat. For example, toggle pause:
```
echo 'cycle pause' | socat - /tmp/mpv-socket
```
For more mpv commands read: https://mpv.io/manual/master/#command-interface

You can also take a look at [scripts](/scripts) page for ideas or refrences.

#### For more info on mpvpaper, please refer the the [man page](/mpvpaper.man).

## Acknowledgments
- glpaper and swaybg for the initial boilerplate code, check em out here:
  - https://hg.sr.ht/~scoopta/glpaper
  - https://github.com/swaywm/swaybg
