The user wants to scrap awww and go back to their original yin daemon setup, but rewritten in Lua to match the existing pattern of Lua scripts for wallpaper management. The key advantage yin had was native video wallpaper support through direct `.mp4` file handling without needing mpv as an intermediary.

Looking at what yin provided that awww lacks: playback control via `--pause`/`--play`, wallpaper restoration with `--restore`, and a set of built-in transitions (bookflip, bounce, box, chessboard, mosaic, static, zoom) accessible through `--list-trans`. The daemon binds to a Unix socket at `/tmp/yin` and maintains per-monitor state files in `~/.cache/yin/` with cached media named by resolution. This native video support is exactly why the awww/swww approach ran into so many problems with mpvpaper layering and race conditions — yin sidesteps all that by handling video directly.

So I need to remove the unused awww package from home.nix, kill both the awww-daemon and any stray swww-daemon processes, then restart yin. Then I'll rewrite the Lua scripts to use yinctl instead: set-wallpaper.lua becomes a single unified call to `yinctl --img <path> --output <monitor> --trans <transition>` (no more branching for video vs image), wallpaper-autostart.lua waits for the socket and applies the boot wallpaper, and wallpaper-picker.lua stays mostly the same since it just feeds selections to set-wallpaper.lua.

I also need to update the transition names in conf/wallpapers.lua to match yin's vocabulary (bookflip, bounce, box, chessboard, mosaic, static, zoom), change hyprland.lua to autostart "yin" instead of "awww-daemon", and since yin and yinctl are already system binaries at /usr/bin, I don't need the absolute-path workaround that awww required. So I don't need a PATH workaround at all — that's a major simplification. For discovering monitors, instead of parsing yin's cache directory like the old bash script did, I can query Hyprland directly with `hyprctl monitors -j` and extract the monitor names, which is much more reliable than relying on cached file quirks.

Now I'm mapping the wallpaper files to yin's transition effects: gojo-eye.mp4 uses zoom, gojo.mp4 uses bookflip, and the static images use the static transition. The valid options are bookflip, bounce, box, chessboard, mosaic, static, and zoom.

The core limitation remains that transitions need genuinely different content to be visible — you can't show a transition between identical images, which is a universal constraint. But videos now get real yin-native transitions instead of the zero transition capability mpvpaper had, so this is a meaningful improvement for video content.

I'm setting up the transition config with specific animations for each video file and deciding whether the single image should use a static transition or something more interesting. Since there's only one image, image-to-image transitions won't show anything regardless, but video-to-image and image-to-video transitions will now work properly with real crossfades and wipes since yin handles both content types uniformly. I'll pick distinct animated transitions for each element to ensure they're all visually different and avoid the "static" default issue — setting latios-latias.png to "chessboard", the default_transition to "bounce", gojo.mp4 to "bookflip", and gojo-eye.mp4to "zoom".

Wait, actually I should preserve the user's original configuration exactly as they had it in their keybinds.lua file — that was their own authored preference, and my job is faithful restoration, not redesign. So I'll honor their original choices: gojo-eye.mp4 stays as "zoom", gojo.mp4 stays as "bookflip", latios-latias.jpg and default both stay as "static" since that's what they originally set. If they want to adjust transitions later, that's their call.

There is one actual bug to fix though: the original config referenced "latios-latias.jpg" but the actual file is "latios-latias.png", so I'll correct that filename mismatch to point at the real file while keeping the "static" transition they originally intended. That's a bug fix, not a taste change.

For the set-wallpaper script, I'm simplifying it to use yin directly since it handles both images and videos natively, eliminating the need for separate branching logic or external tools.

Writing the Lua script... Writing wallpaper setup logic...

Actually, I'm realizing there's a problem with how I'm handling the background processes — each `os.execute()` call spawns its own shell subprocess, so backgrounding commands with `&` doesn't actually keep them running together the way I intended, since they're not sharing a job table across separate shell invocations. The real solution is to build a single shell command string containing all the backgrounded yinctl calls plus a trailing `wait`, then execute that entire string as one os.execute() call so the backgrounding and waiting happen within the same shell instance. I'm restructuring the code to collect all the monitor commands into a table and then join them into one cohesive shell invocation. I'm reconsidering whether the parallel-with-wait complexity is even worth it, since yinctl calls are probably fast local IPC operations anyway. But the original script deliberately parallelized for a reason—especially if videos take time to initialize—so I'll stick with that pattern, just making sure it's implemented correctly as a single shell invocation. I also need to handle the fallback case when no monitors are found, which should invoke yinctl without the --output flag to let it use the default display.

For the wallpaper-autostart script, I'm translating the bash approach into Lua: it'll poll for yin's Unix socket at /tmp/yin (yin's fixed socket path, unlike awww which had no standard location) and apply the boot image once the socket is ready.

Writing Lua socket polling... Writing Lua utility functions... Writing yinctl execution logic... Updating the hyprland.lua autostart to call yin directly instead of the absolute path to awww-daemon, since yin is already available on Hyprland's PATH. The wallpaper-picker.lua doesn't need any changes since it's backend-agnostic. I should remove the awww package from home.nix and run home-manager switch to clean it up.

For the process cleanup, I need to kill both the awww-daemon and the stray swww-daemon that was started during testing — since we're fully switching back to yin, both should be removed as part of the complete cutover.

Then I'll start the yin daemon (either detached or through a supervised process like I did with awww) and wait for the socket to appear before applying the boot wallpaper to get to a clean, working state.

I should also verify the cached yin state in ~/.cache/yin still exists from earlier, though it's likely stale and yin will handle recreating it as needed — and I'm reconsidering whether to clean up the existing Lua script files since they're already in place.

Now I'm ready to execute: update home.nix to remove awww, switch home-manager, kill the old daemons, rewrite the wallpaper config and scripts to use yin's transition names and fix that latios-latias.jpg typo, then update the remaining script files. Starting with `yinctl --list-trans` to get the authoritative list of valid transition names rather than relying on memory, and I'll wrap it in a timeout since bare `yin` hung earlier — but `yinctl` is the client binary so it should be safe and quick.

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Usage: set-wallpaper.lua <path> [transition]
-- Applies the wallpaper via yin/yinctl, which handles both images and
-- videos natively -- no separate video player, no per-type branching.
-- Transition is looked up in conf/wallpapers.lua when not passed explicitly.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local wallpaper = arg[1]
local transition = arg[2]
if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
    io.stderr:write("Usage: set-wallpaper.lua <path> [transition]\n")
    os.exit(1)
end

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

if not transition or transition == "" then
    transition = wallpapers.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers.default_transition

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Applies the boot wallpaper once yin's IPC socket is ready.
--
-- yin is started by Hyprland's autostart (see hyprland.lua) immediately
-- before this script. It binds a Unix socket at /tmp/yin once it comes up,
-- so instead of guessing with a fixed delay, this waits for that socket to
-- exist before calling yinctl, so yinctl never races the daemon.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
local IMG = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/wallpapers/latios-latias.png"
local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-autostart.log"
local SOCKET = "/tmp/yin"

local SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 -- give up waiting for the socket after ~5s
local RETRIES = 20             -- then retry the apply loop this many times (0.1s apart)
local POLL_MS = 100

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
    if type(ok) == "number" then
        return ok == 0
    end
    return ok == true
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. sh(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-autostart] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

log(string.format("starting; waiting for yin socket at %s (timeout %dms)", SOCKET, SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS))

-- 1. Wait for yin to create its IPC socket.
local waited = 0
while not exec_ok("[ -S " .. sh(SOCKET) .. " ]") do
    if waited >= SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS then
        log(string.format("ERROR: yin socket did not appear within %dms; aborting", SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS))
        os.exit(1)
    end
    os.execute("sleep 0.1")
    waited = waited + POLL_MS
end
log(string.format("yin socket ready after %dms", waited))

-- 2. Discover the monitors this Hyprland instance actually has.
local monitors = {}
local p = io.popen("hyprctl monitors -j 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].name' 2>/dev/null")
if p then
    for line in p:lines() do
        if line ~= "" then table.insert(monitors, line) end
    end
    p:close()
end
if #monitors == 0 then
    log("WARN: hyprctl reported no monitors; falling back to yin's default output")
end

-- 3. Apply the wallpaper to each monitor, retrying until every one succeeds.
local attempt = 1
while true do
    local all_ok = true
    if #monitors == 0 then
        if not exec_ok("yinctl --img " .. sh(IMG) .. " >> " .. sh(LOG) .. " 2>&1") then
            all_ok = false
        end
    else
        for _, m in ipairs(monitors) do
            if not exec_ok("yinctl --img " .. sh(IMG) .. " --output " .. sh(m) .. " >> " .. sh(LOG) .. " 2>&1") then
                all_ok = false
                log(string.format("yinctl for '%s' failed on attempt %d", m, attempt))
            end
        end
    end

    if all_ok then
        log(string.format("wallpaper applied on attempt %d (img=%s)", attempt, IMG))
        os.exit(0)
    end
    if attempt >= RETRIES then
        log(string.format("ERROR: wallpaper apply failed after %d attempts", attempt))
        os.exit(1)
    end
    attempt = attempt + 1
    os.execute("sleep 0.1")
end

    hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_cmd("yin"))

    hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_cmd("/home/krubics/.nix-profile/bin/hyprsession"))

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Persistent listener: reapplies the current wallpaper to any monitor that
-- appears after Hyprland starts (hotplug reconnect, or a monitor coming
-- back on). yin discovers new monitors fine on its own but never
-- automatically re-applies a wallpaper to them -- something has to call
-- yinctl explicitly, every time, for every monitor. This listens on
-- Hyprland's own IPC event socket for "monitoraddedv2" and does that.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local XDG_RUNTIME_DIR = os.getenv("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")
local SIG = os.getenv("HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE")
local SOCKET = XDG_RUNTIME_DIR .. "/hypr/" .. SIG .. "/.socket2.sock"

local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-hotplug.log"

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. sh(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-hotplug] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function apply_current(monitor)
    local p = io.popen("readlink -f " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper") .. " 2>/dev/null")
    local wallpaper = p and p:read("*l") or nil
    if p then p:close() end

    if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
        log("no current-wallpaper set yet, skipping " .. monitor)
        return
    end

    local transition = wallpapers.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers.default_transition
    log(("applying %s to %s (%s)"):format(wallpaper, monitor, transition))
    os.execute(("yinctl --img %s --trans %s --output %s >> %s 2>&1"):format(
        sh(wallpaper), sh(transition), sh(monitor), sh(LOG)
    ))
end

if not SIG then
    log("ERROR: HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE not set; aborting")
    os.exit(1)
end

log("starting; listening on " .. SOCKET)

local events = io.popen("socat -u UNIX-CONNECT:" .. sh(SOCKET) .. " -")
if not events then
    log("ERROR: failed to open event socket")
    os.exit(1)
end

for line in events:lines() do
    local name = line:match("^monitoraddedv2>>%d+,([^,]+),")
    if name then
        log("monitor added: " .. name)
        apply_current(name)
    end
end

log("event stream closed; exiting")

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Persistent listener: reapplies the current wallpaper to any monitor that
-- appears after Hyprland starts (hotplug reconnect, or a monitor coming
-- back on). yin discovers new monitors fine on its own but never
-- automatically re-applies a wallpaper to them -- something has to call
-- yinctl explicitly, every time, for every monitor. This listens on
-- Hyprland's own IPC event socket for "monitoraddedv2" and does that.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local XDG_RUNTIME_DIR = os.getenv("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")
local SIG = os.getenv("HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE")
local SOCKET = XDG_RUNTIME_DIR .. "/hypr/" .. SIG .. "/.socket2.sock"

local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-hotplug.log"

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. sh(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-hotplug] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function apply_current(monitor)
    local p = io.popen("readlink -f " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper") .. " 2>/dev/null")
    local wallpaper = p and p:read("*l") or nil
    if p then p:close() end

    if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
        log("no current-wallpaper set yet, skipping " .. monitor)
        return
    end

    local transition = wallpapers.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers.default_transition
    log(("applying %s to %s (%s)"):format(wallpaper, monitor, transition))
    os.execute(("yinctl --img %s --trans %s --output %s >> %s 2>&1"):format(
        sh(wallpaper), sh(transition), sh(monitor), sh(LOG)
    ))
end

if not SIG then
    log("ERROR: HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE not set; aborting")
    os.exit(1)
end

log("starting; listening on " .. SOCKET)

local events = io.popen("socat -u UNIX-CONNECT:" .. sh(SOCKET) .. " -")
if not events then
    log("ERROR: failed to open event socket")
    os.exit(1)
end

for line in events:lines() do
    local name = line:match("^monitoraddedv2>>%d+,([^,]+),")
    if name then
        log("monitor added: " .. name)
        apply_current(name)
    end
end

log("event stream closed; exiting")

Since there's no direct way to query Yin about what it knows, the best approach is to implement a retry-with-backoff pattern on the yinctl call itself—attempt it, check the exit code, and retry a few times with short delays if it fails. I'll use the same pattern as wallpaper-autostart.lua with a reasonable timeout (20 retries at 100ms intervals gives about 2 seconds total), which should be enough for Yin's internal registration to catch up.

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Persistent listener: reapplies the current wallpaper to any monitor that
-- appears after Hyprland starts (hotplug reconnect, or a monitor coming
-- back on). yin discovers new monitors fine on its own but never
-- automatically re-applies a wallpaper to them -- something has to call
-- yinctl explicitly, every time, for every monitor. This listens on
-- Hyprland's own IPC event socket for "monitoraddedv2" and does that.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local XDG_RUNTIME_DIR = os.getenv("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")
local SIG = os.getenv("HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE")
local SOCKET = XDG_RUNTIME_DIR .. "/hypr/" .. SIG .. "/.socket2.sock"

local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-hotplug.log"

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. sh(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-hotplug] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
    if type(ok) == "number" then
        return ok == 0
    end
    return ok == true
end

local function apply_current(monitor)
    local p = io.popen("readlink -f " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper") .. " 2>/dev/null")
    local wallpaper = p and p:read("*l") or nil
    if p then p:close() end

    if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
        log("no current-wallpaper set yet, skipping " .. monitor)
        return
    end

    local transition = wallpapers.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers.default_transition
    local cmd = ("yinctl --img %s --trans %s --output %s >> %s 2>&1"):format(
        sh(wallpaper), sh(transition), sh(monitor), sh(LOG)
    )

    -- Hyprland fires this event as soon as *it* knows about the monitor,
    -- which can be a beat before yin's own (separate) Wayland connection
    -- has registered it -- yinctl aborts with "Could not find required
    -- monitor" if called too early, so retry briefly instead of assuming
    -- yin is already caught up.
    local RETRIES, POLL_MS = 15, 200
    for attempt = 1, RETRIES do
        if exec_ok(cmd) then
            log(("applied %s to %s (%s) on attempt %d"):format(wallpaper, monitor, transition, attempt))
            return
        end
        os.execute("sleep 0.2")
    end
    log(("ERROR: failed to apply wallpaper to %s after %d attempts"):format(monitor, RETRIES))
end

if not SIG then
    log("ERROR: HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE not set; aborting")
    os.exit(1)
end

log("starting; listening on " .. SOCKET)

local events = io.popen("socat -u UNIX-CONNECT:" .. sh(SOCKET) .. " -")
if not events then
    log("ERROR: failed to open event socket")
    os.exit(1)
end

for line in events:lines() do
    local name = line:match("^monitoraddedv2>>%d+,([^,]+),")
    if name then
        log("monitor added: " .. name)
        apply_current(name)
    end
end

log("event stream closed; exiting")

## Confirmed and built

**`scripts/wallpaper-hotplug.lua`** — persistent listener, wired into `hyprland.lua`'s autostart:
- Connects to Hyprland's own IPC event socket (`.socket2.sock`), watches for `monitoraddedv2>>ID,NAME,DESC`
- On a new monitor, reads `~/.cache/current-wallpaper` (already maintained by `set-wallpaper.lua`) and looks up its transition from `conf/wallpapers.lua`
- Runs `yinctl --img <current> --trans <transition> --output <new-monitor>`, retrying up to 15× (200ms apart) to absorb one real race: **Hyprland fires its IPC event slightly before `yin`'s own separate Wayland connection has registered the same output**, so an immediate `yinctl --output <name>` aborts with `Could not find required monitor`. Retry #2 always caught it in testing.

**Verified live**, three scenarios, via `hyprctl output create/remove headless` (genuine `wl_registry` add/remove, same as real hardware):
1. Fresh monitor appears, image is current → auto-applied, screenshotted.
2. Same, but confirmed the race actually happens and the retry recovers it (log shows attempt 1 crash, attempt 2 success).
3. Fresh monitor appears, **video** is current → correctly triggers `yin`'s own per-resolution transcode (this specific video had never been cached at that resolution, took ~23s), then applied. Not a bug — first-time-per-resolution cost is inherent to `yin`, and it's a one-time cost per (video, resolution) pair.

One thing worth flagging: on a real multi-monitor setup where you already use the *same* resolution across your outputs, reconnects will be instant (cache hit) — the 23s case only happens for a genuinely new resolution the video's never been shown at.

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Persistent listener: reapplies the current wallpaper to any monitor that
-- appears after Hyprland starts (hotplug reconnect, or a monitor coming
-- back on). yin discovers new monitors fine on its own but never
-- automatically re-applies a wallpaper to them -- something has to call
-- yinctl explicitly, every time, for every monitor. This listens on
-- Hyprland's own IPC event socket for "monitoraddedv2" and does that.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local XDG_RUNTIME_DIR = os.getenv("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")
local SIG = os.getenv("HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE")
local SOCKET = XDG_RUNTIME_DIR .. "/hypr/" .. SIG .. "/.socket2.sock"

local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-hotplug.log"

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. sh(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-hotplug] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
    if type(ok) == "number" then
        return ok == 0
    end
    return ok == true
end

local function apply_current(monitor)
    local p = io.popen("readlink -f " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper") .. " 2>/dev/null")
    local wallpaper = p and p:read("*l") or nil
    if p then p:close() end

    if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
        log("no current-wallpaper set yet, skipping " .. monitor)
        return
    end

    local transition = wallpapers.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers.default_transition
    local cmd = ("yinctl --img %s --trans %s --output %s >> %s 2>&1"):format(
        sh(wallpaper), sh(transition), sh(monitor), sh(LOG)
    )

    -- Hyprland fires this event as soon as *it* knows about the monitor,
    -- which can be a beat before yin's own (separate) Wayland connection
    -- has registered it -- yinctl aborts with "Could not find required
    -- monitor" if called too early, so retry briefly instead of assuming
    -- yin is already caught up.
    local RETRIES, POLL_MS = 15, 200
    for attempt = 1, RETRIES do
        if exec_ok(cmd) then
            log(("applied %s to %s (%s) on attempt %d"):format(wallpaper, monitor, transition, attempt))
            return
        end
        os.execute("sleep 0.2")
    end
    log(("ERROR: failed to apply wallpaper to %s after %d attempts"):format(monitor, RETRIES))
end

if not SIG then
    log("ERROR: HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE not set; aborting")
    os.exit(1)
end

log("starting; listening on " .. SOCKET)

local events = io.popen("socat -u UNIX-CONNECT:" .. sh(SOCKET) .. " -")
if not events then
    log("ERROR: failed to open event socket")
    os.exit(1)
end

for line in events:lines() do
    local name = line:match("^monitoraddedv2>>%d+,([^,]+),")
    if name then
        log("monitor added: " .. name)
        apply_current(name)
    end
end

log("event stream closed; exiting")

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Persistent listener: reapplies the current wallpaper to any monitor that
-- appears after Hyprland starts (hotplug reconnect, or a monitor coming
-- back on). yin discovers new monitors fine on its own but never
-- automatically re-applies a wallpaper to them -- something has to call
-- yinctl explicitly, every time, for every monitor. This listens on
-- Hyprland's own IPC event socket for "monitoraddedv2" and does that.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local XDG_RUNTIME_DIR = os.getenv("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")
local SIG = os.getenv("HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE")
local SOCKET = XDG_RUNTIME_DIR .. "/hypr/" .. SIG .. "/.socket2.sock"

local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-hotplug.log"

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. sh(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
…
    end
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
…
    return ok == true
end

local function apply_current(monitor)
    local p = io.popen("readlink -f " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper") .. " 2>/dev/null")
…
    log(("ERROR: failed to apply wallpaper to %s after %d attempts"):format(monitor, RETRIES))
end

local function main()
    if not SIG then
…
    log("event stream closed")
end

-- The hyprland.lua dispatch respawns this script on exit, but that only
-- helps if a crash actually gets logged instead of vanishing -- catch
-- anything unexpected here so the next run has a real reason to go on,
-- not just silence.
local ok, err = pcall(main)
if not ok then
    log("CRASHED: " .. tostring(err))
end

    local p = io.popen("readlink -f " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper") .. " 2>/dev/null")

    -- yin is already caught up.

            return
        end
        os.execute("sleep 0.2")
    end

end

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Persistent listener: reapplies the current wallpaper to any monitor that
-- appears after Hyprland starts (hotplug reconnect, or a monitor coming
-- back on). yin discovers new monitors fine on its own but never
-- automatically re-applies a wallpaper to them -- something has to call
-- yinctl explicitly, every time, for every monitor. This listens on
-- Hyprland's own IPC event socket for "monitoraddedv2" and does that.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local XDG_RUNTIME_DIR = os.getenv("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")
local SIG = os.getenv("HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE")
local SOCKET = XDG_RUNTIME_DIR .. "/hypr/" .. SIG .. "/.socket2.sock"

local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-hotplug.log"

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. sh(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-hotplug] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function exec_ok(cmd)
    local ok = os.execute(cmd)
    if type(ok) == "number" then
        return ok == 0
    end
    return ok == true
end

local function apply_current(monitor)
    local p = io.popen("readlink -f " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper") .. " 2>/dev/null")
    local wallpaper = p and p:read("*l") or nil
    if p then p:close() end

    if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
        log("no current-wallpaper set yet, skipping " .. monitor)
        return
    end

    local transition = wallpapers.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers.default_transition
    local cmd = ("yinctl --img %s --trans %s --output %s >> %s 2>&1"):format(
        sh(wallpaper), sh(transition), sh(monitor), sh(LOG)
    )

    -- Hyprland fires this event as soon as *it* knows about the monitor,
    -- which can be a beat before yin's own (separate) Wayland connection
    -- has registered it -- yinctl aborts with "Could not find required
    -- monitor" if called too early, so retry briefly instead of assuming
    -- yin is already caught up.
    local RETRIES, POLL_MS = 15, 200
    for attempt = 1, RETRIES do
        if exec_ok(cmd) then
            log(("applied %s to %s (%s) on attempt %d"):format(wallpaper, monitor, transition, attempt))
            return
        end
        os.execute("sleep 0.2")
    end
    log(("ERROR: failed to apply wallpaper to %s after %d attempts"):format(monitor, RETRIES))
end

local function main()
    if not SIG then
        log("ERROR: HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE not set; aborting")
        os.exit(1)
    end

    log("starting; listening on " .. SOCKET)

    local events = io.popen("socat -u UNIX-CONNECT:" .. sh(SOCKET) .. " -")
    if not events then
        log("ERROR: failed to open event socket")
        return
    end

    for line in events:lines() do
        local name = line:match("^monitoraddedv2>>%d+,([^,]+),")
        if name then
            log("monitor added: " .. name)
            apply_current(name)
        end
    end

    log("event stream closed")
end

-- The hyprland.lua dispatch respawns this script on exit, but that only
-- helps if a crash actually gets logged instead of vanishing -- catch
-- anything unexpected here so the next run has a real reason to go on,
-- not just silence.
local ok, err = pcall(main)
if not ok then
    log("CRASHED: " .. tostring(err))
end

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Persistent listener: reapplies the current wallpaper to any monitor that
-- appears after Hyprland starts (hotplug reconnect, or a monitor coming
-- back on). yin discovers new monitors fine on its own but never
-- automatically re-applies a wallpaper to them -- something has to call
-- yinctl explicitly, every time, for every monitor. This listens on
-- Hyprland's own IPC event socket for "monitoraddedv2" and does that.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local XDG_RUNTIME_DIR = os.getenv("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")
local SIG = os.getenv("HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE")
local SOCKET = XDG_RUNTIME_DIR .. "/hypr/" .. SIG .. "/.socket2.sock"

local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-hotplug.log"

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. sh(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-hotplug] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function apply_current(monitor)
    local p = io.popen("readlink -f " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper") .. " 2>/dev/null")
    local wallpaper = p and p:read("*l") or nil
    if p then p:close() end

    if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
        log("no current-wallpaper set yet, skipping " .. monitor)
        return
    end

    -- No --output: yinctl with a bare --img applies to every monitor yin
    -- currently knows about, including one that just appeared moments ago.
    -- Targeting the new monitor by name raced yin's own (separate) Wayland
    -- connection registering it and crashed ("Could not find required
    -- monitor") if called too early; the untargeted form doesn't have that
    -- problem, at the cost of replaying the transition on every monitor
    -- each time one is added, not just the new one.
    local transition = wallpapers.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers.default_transition
    local cmd = ("yinctl --img %s --trans %s >> %s 2>&1"):format(sh(wallpaper), sh(transition), sh(LOG))
    log(("applying %s (%s), triggered by %s"):format(wallpaper, transition, monitor))
    os.execute(cmd)
end

local function main()
    if not SIG then
        log("ERROR: HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE not set; aborting")
        os.exit(1)
    end

    log("starting; listening on " .. SOCKET)

    local events = io.popen("socat -u UNIX-CONNECT:" .. sh(SOCKET) .. " -")
    if not events then
        log("ERROR: failed to open event socket")
        return
    end

    for line in events:lines() do
        local name = line:match("^monitoraddedv2>>%d+,([^,]+),")
        if name then
            log("monitor added: " .. name)
            apply_current(name)
        end
    end

    log("event stream closed")
end

-- The hyprland.lua dispatch respawns this script on exit, but that only
-- helps if a crash actually gets logged instead of vanishing -- catch
-- anything unexpected here so the next run has a real reason to go on,
-- not just silence.
local ok, err = pcall(main)
if not ok then
    log("CRASHED: " .. tostring(err))
end

    -- Targeting the new monitor by name raced yin's own (separate) Wayland
    -- connection registering it and crashed ("Could not find required
    -- monitor") if called too early; the untargeted form doesn't have that
    -- problem, at the cost of replaying the transition on every monitor
    -- each time one is added, not just the new one.

        os.exit(1)
    end

    log("starting; listening on " .. SOCKET)

    local events = io.popen("socat -u UNIX-CONNECT:" .. sh(SOCKET) .. " -")
    if not events then
        log("ERROR: failed to open event socket")

            apply_current(name)

    log("event stream closed")

-- anything unexpected here so the next run has a real reason to go on,
-- not just silence.

#!/usr/bin/env lua
-- Persistent listener: reapplies the current wallpaper to any monitor that
-- appears after Hyprland starts (hotplug reconnect, or a monitor coming
-- back on). yin discovers new monitors fine on its own but never
-- automatically re-applies a wallpaper to them -- something has to call
-- yinctl explicitly, every time, for every monitor. This listens on
-- Hyprland's own IPC event socket for "monitoraddedv2" and does that.

local HOME = os.getenv("HOME")
package.path = HOME .. "/.config/hypr/?.lua;" .. package.path
local wallpapers = require("conf.wallpapers")

local XDG_RUNTIME_DIR = os.getenv("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")
local SIG = os.getenv("HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE")
local SOCKET = XDG_RUNTIME_DIR .. "/hypr/" .. SIG .. "/.socket2.sock"

local STATE_HOME = os.getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME") or (HOME .. "/.local/state")
local LOG = STATE_HOME .. "/hypr/wallpaper-hotplug.log"

local function sh(s)
    return "'" .. s:gsub("'", "'\\''") .. "'"
end

local function basename(path)
    return path:match("([^/]+)$") or path
end

os.execute("mkdir -p " .. sh(LOG:match("(.*)/") or "."))

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(string.format("%s [wallpaper-hotplug] %s\n", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), msg))
        f:close()
    end
end

local function mtime(path)
    local p = io.popen("stat -c %Y " .. sh(path) .. " 2>/dev/null")
    local t = p and p:read("*l") or nil
    if p then p:close() end
    return t
end

local function apply_current(monitor)
    local p = io.popen("readlink -f " .. sh(HOME .. "/.cache/current-wallpaper") .. " 2>/dev/null")
    local wallpaper = p and p:read("*l") or nil
    if p then p:close() end

    if not wallpaper or wallpaper == "" then
        log("no current-wallpaper set yet, skipping " .. monitor)
        return
    end

    -- No --output: a bare --img applies to every monitor yin currently
    -- knows about, including one that just appeared moments ago -- at the
    -- cost of replaying the transition on every other monitor too, not
    -- just the new one. Targeting the new monitor by name used to crash
    -- ("Could not find required monitor") if yin's own Wayland connection
    -- hadn't registered it yet; dropping --output avoids that crash, but
    -- doesn't avoid the underlying race -- yin just silently drops any
    -- monitor it doesn't know about yet instead of erroring, so it still
    -- needs confirming via yin's own per-monitor cache file (its mtime
    -- moves only if that specific monitor was actually reached) and
    -- retrying if the new monitor didn't get it.
    local transition = wallpapers.transitions[basename(wallpaper)] or wallpapers.default_transition
    local cmd = ("yinctl --img %s --trans %s >> %s 2>&1"):format(sh(wallpaper), sh(transition), sh(LOG))
    local cache_file = HOME .. "/.cache/yin/" .. monitor

    local RETRIES, POLL_MS = 15, 200
    for attempt = 1, RETRIES do
        local before = mtime(cache_file)
        os.execute(cmd)
        os.execute("sleep 0.1")
        local after = mtime(cache_file)
        if after and after ~= before then
            log(("applied %s (%s), confirmed on %s on attempt %d"):format(wallpaper, transition, monitor, attempt))
            return
        end
        os.execute("sleep 0.1")
    end
    log(("ERROR: %s never showed the wallpaper after %d attempts"):format(monitor, RETRIES))
end

local function main()
    if not SIG then
        log("ERROR: HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE not set; aborting")
        os.exit(1)
    end

    log("starting; listening on " .. SOCKET)

    local events = io.popen("socat -u UNIX-CONNECT:" .. sh(SOCKET) .. " -")
    if not events then
        log("ERROR: failed to open event socket")
        return
    end

    for line in events:lines() do
        local name = line:match("^monitoraddedv2>>%d+,([^,]+),")
        if name then
            log("monitor added: " .. name)
            apply_current(name)
        end
    end

    log("event stream closed")
end

-- The hyprland.lua dispatch respawns this script on exit, but that only
-- helps if a crash actually gets logged instead of vanishing -- catch
-- anything unexpected here so the next run has a real reason to go on,
-- not just silence.
local ok, err = pcall(main)
if not ok then
    log("CRASHED: " .. tostring(err))
end

## Summary

Dropped `--output`, but **not silently** — it exposed a worse failure mode than what it fixed, so I found and fixed that too before calling it done.

**What changed in `wallpaper-hotplug.lua`**: `yinctl --img <current> --trans <transition>` — no `--output`, applies to every monitor `yin` currently knows about, new one included.

**But**: dropping `--output` alone doesn't fix the underlying race, it just changes how it fails. Confirmed empirically:
- Targeted (`--output <name>`): races `yin`'s own Wayland registration → **crashes loudly** (`Could not find required monitor`) if called too early. Easy to detect and retry.
- Untargeted (bare `--img`): same race, but instead of erring it **silently omits** any monitor `yin` hasn't registered yet — exit 0, no error, new monitor just never gets the wallpaper. Reproduced 4/4 failures with the listener reacting at full speed to the IPC event.

**Fix**: check `yin`'s own per-monitor cache file (`~/.cache/yin/<name>`) mtime before/after the call, retry (same 15×200ms budget as before) until it actually moves for that monitor. Keeps your "no `--output`" simplification while catching the case it silently drops.

**Verified**: stress-tested across multiple hotplug cycles — 4/5 succeeded on attempt 1-2 once confirmed via mtime. The one failure was `yin` itself crashing (`Could not connect to Ipc socket`) under my test loop hammering 5 rapid headless create/destroy cycles in ~16s — unrelated to this script, and far faster than any real-world hotplug would ever fire. Restarted `yin`, reran a single realistic event cleanly, screenshotted the result.

Net effect vs. the `--output` version: same reliability, but now every hotplug replays the transition across *all* your monitors instead of just the new one — that's the real tradeoff of dropping `--output`, not the race (which needed fixing either way).
